# Source: README.md

# Momo documentation

Momo is a Go ORM that generates typed column and relation descriptors from
plain Go structs, keeps SQL explicit and inspectable, builds pgvector support
into the core API, and ships its own migration engine that writes reviewable
SQL. It supports PostgreSQL with pgvector; [capabilities](capabilities.md)
states exactly what else exists and what does not. Pages are written from the
code and checked in CI: every Go block compiles, and the examples run against
PostgreSQL.

New here? Start with [getting started](getting-started.md).

## Pages

- [Getting started](getting-started.md): requirements, install, a first program that talks to PostgreSQL, and where the typed API starts.
- [Guide for AI coding agents](ai-guide.md): one self-contained file for an agent using Momo in an application: setup, modeling, migrations, queries, relations, vectors, errors, testing, known pitfalls and rules. Also indexed by `llms.txt` at the repository root.
- [Go to SQL type mapping](TYPE_MAPPING.md): column type per Go type, edge values, null handling.
- [Vector search](vectors.md): pgvector types, metrics, limits, search settings and the binary codec.
- [MySQL and MariaDB](mysql.md): supported servers, DSN requirements, the capability matrix, write and locking differences, error mapping, and what is not available yet.
- [Full-text search](fulltext.md): declaring a search on a model, what each dialect creates, the portable search, score and snippet calls, the comparison table and limits, the PostgreSQL tsvector builders, and hybrid vector plus text search.
- [Projections](projections.md): declaring a projection, `From` and `Columns`, the generated metadata, tuple rows (`Row1` to `Row10`), the soft-delete filter.
- [Relations](relations.md): declaring, loading, filtering and writing relations, with error behavior and limits.
- [Migration safety and recovery](migrations.md): snapshots, apply semantics, locks, failure recovery, production checklist, CLI reference.
- [Audit history tables](history.md): `Config.History`, the history table, function and trigger the generator declares, the actor of a transaction, the versions of a row and its state at a time, schema changes, and `generate --from-db`.
- [Importing models from other ORMs](importers.md): the GORM, Bun and Ent readers (static, they never execute your code), the `momo import` command, the import report and what each report kind means, and the readers that import Atlas, goose, golang-migrate and Bun migration history.
- [Coming from GORM](guides/gorm.md): a call-by-call cheat sheet from GORM models, queries, relations, hooks, transactions, migrations and errors to Momo.
- [Coming from Bun](guides/bun.md): the same mapping for Bun users.
- [Coming from Ent](guides/ent.md): the same mapping for Ent users, with the `momo import ent` path.
- [LISTEN and NOTIFY](listen-notify.md): `pgxdriver.Listen` and `pgxdriver.Notify`, reconnecting, and payload limits.
- [Transactional outbox](outbox.md): `outbox.Outbox.Add` in the caller's transaction, the relay with leases, retries, per-key order and retention, and waking it with `LISTEN`.
- [Read replicas](replicas.md): `WithReplicas`, which statements go to a replica, reading your own writes, and what happens when a replica is down.
- [Testing applications](testing.md): the `momotest` kit: a schema or a rolled-back transaction per test, migrations applied, fixture seeding, parallel-safe.
- [Interceptors](PRIVACY_RULES.md): application-level per-handle rules that add predicates or deny typed statements, the tenant recipe, and the paths they do not cover (not a security boundary).
- [Static check for raw SQL](momovet.md): the momovet analyzer that reports non-constant SQL passed to the raw-SQL functions.
- [Observability hooks](observability.md): the `obs` package: the test recorder, the N+1 relation-load and statement detectors and the `momolog` slog hook, and how they treat sensitive arguments.
- [Capabilities](capabilities.md): what each database supports, what is not built, and what returns `ErrUnsupported`.
- [Performance](PERFORMANCE.md): the measured hook-overhead allocation budget and the layout of the comparison benchmark suite.
- [Supported versions](supported-versions.md): Go, PostgreSQL, pgvector, PgBouncer, pgx and OS versions in CI for v0.19.0, and the stability policy. <!-- x-release-please-version -->
- [Using these docs with an AI coding agent](agents.md): where an agent should read, canonical patterns and a copy-paste AGENTS.md snippet.
- [API reference](reference.md): every exported identifier of the core and feature packages with its doc-comment synopsis; generated by `go generate`.
- [Architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md): the packages that exist, how they layer and the import rules the tests enforce.
- [Compatibility and deprecation policy](compatibility.md): what the v1 promise covers and excludes, how a deprecated API is retired, the apidiff gate, and how pre-v1 releases differ.
- [Upgrading](upgrading.md): breaking changes between releases, with a rewrite recipe; pre-v1, so more can follow.
- [Contributing](contributing.md): prerequisites, test commands, commit messages and file headers.

## Examples

Runnable programs, each tested end to end in CI. See [the examples index](../examples/README.md) for the layout and how to add one.

- [quickstart](../examples/quickstart/): the root README loop: models, generate, CRUD, relations, vector search, a transaction.
- [crud-zero-null](../examples/crud-zero-null/): insert, update, delete; zero value versus NULL versus default; soft delete.
- [transactions](../examples/transactions/): Tx, rollback, savepoints, read-only and isolation, retry on serialization failure.
- [testing](../examples/testing/): momotest: a database or a rolled-back transaction per test, migrations applied, seeded fixtures, parallel tests.
- [relations](../examples/relations/): has-many, belongs-to, many-to-many; Load, Preload, Joined, Has, Link, CreateGraph.
- [projection-pagination](../examples/projection-pagination/): column subsets, keyset pagination with a tie-break, counting.
- [vector-search](../examples/vector-search/): HNSW index, nearest-neighbour queries, filters, search settings.
- [upgrade-database](../examples/upgrade-database/): change a model after production: add a column with a default, add an index, rename a column, apply with data kept, generate --check and drift.
- [custom-sql-migration](../examples/custom-sql-migration/): hand-written SQL migrations beside generated ones: backfill, DO $$ splitting, -- momo:no-transaction, a hand-written CONCURRENTLY index, momo.sum checksums.
- [adopt-existing-schema](../examples/adopt-existing-schema/): put a plain-SQL database under Momo with migrate baseline (`momo generate --from-db` can then write the models from the database).


# Source: getting-started.md

# Getting started

This page takes you from an empty module to a program that talks to
PostgreSQL through Momo. It stays small on purpose: the first program uses no
generated code. The full loop (models, `momo generate`, migrations, typed
queries, relations, vector search) is the
[quickstart example](../examples/quickstart/), which is compiled and run
end to end in CI.

## Requirements

- Go 1.26 or newer.
- PostgreSQL with the pgvector extension installed on the server. The other
  databases, and the dialects the `momo migrate` command runs, are listed in
  the generated status of [capabilities](capabilities.md).
- A role that may create extensions, or a superuser who runs
  `CREATE EXTENSION vector` once in the target database. The first generated
  migration creates the extension when a model has a vector column.

## Install

Add the library to your module and install the CLI at the same version:

```sh
go get github.com/azrtydxb/momo@latest
go install github.com/azrtydxb/momo/cmd/momo@latest
```

Pin an explicit version instead of `latest` in a real project, and keep the CLI
and the library on the same one. The supported Go and PostgreSQL versions are
listed in [supported versions](supported-versions.md).

## Connect and run SQL

`pgxdriver.Open` opens a pgx pool and returns a Momo driver that owns it, and
`momo.New` returns the `*momo.DB`. `db.Close` closes the pool. Every driver
package has the same two constructors: `Open(ctx, dsn, opts...)` opens the
database and owns it, and `New(handle, opts...)` wraps a pool or `*sql.DB` you
opened, so `db.Close` leaves it alone and you close it.

`db.Tx` runs a function in a transaction and commits when it returns nil.
Inside it, use the `tx` handle for every statement. `momo.Exec` and
`momo.QueryScalars` are the raw SQL path: `?` binds the next argument, so values
never become part of the SQL text.

The program reads the connection string from `MOMO_EXAMPLE_DSN`, for example
`postgres://user:pass@localhost:5432/scratch?sslmode=disable`. It creates a
temporary table inside the transaction, so it leaves nothing behind.

<!-- docscheck:run -->

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"log"
	"os"

	"github.com/azrtydxb/momo"
	"github.com/azrtydxb/momo/driver/pgxdriver"
)

func main() {
	if err := run(context.Background()); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}

func run(ctx context.Context) error {
	drv, err := pgxdriver.Open(ctx, os.Getenv("MOMO_EXAMPLE_DSN"))
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	db := momo.New(drv)
	defer db.Close()

	return db.Tx(ctx, momo.TxOptions{}, func(tx *momo.Tx) error {
		if _, err := momo.Exec(ctx, tx, "CREATE TEMP TABLE notes (id bigint PRIMARY KEY, body text NOT NULL)"); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if _, err := momo.Exec(ctx, tx, "INSERT INTO notes (id, body) VALUES (?, ?)", 1, "hello"); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		bodies, err := momo.QueryScalars[string](ctx, tx, "SELECT body FROM notes WHERE id = ?", 1)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		fmt.Println(bodies)
		return nil
	})
}
```

## Handle errors

Momo classifies database errors into sentinels. Compare with `errors.Is`, never
with error text. This program violates a primary key on purpose and branches on
`momo.ErrUniqueViolation`; the transaction rolls back when the function returns
the error, so the table disappears with it.

<!-- docscheck:run -->

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"log"
	"os"

	"github.com/azrtydxb/momo"
	"github.com/azrtydxb/momo/driver/pgxdriver"
)

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	drv, err := pgxdriver.Open(ctx, os.Getenv("MOMO_EXAMPLE_DSN"))
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	db := momo.New(drv)
	defer db.Close()

	err = db.Tx(ctx, momo.TxOptions{}, func(tx *momo.Tx) error {
		if _, err := momo.Exec(ctx, tx, "CREATE TEMP TABLE tags (name text PRIMARY KEY)"); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		for range 2 {
			if _, err := momo.Exec(ctx, tx, "INSERT INTO tags (name) VALUES (?)", "go"); err != nil {
				return err
			}
		}
		return nil
	})
	if !errors.Is(err, momo.ErrUniqueViolation) {
		log.Fatalf("want a unique violation, got %v", err)
	}
	fmt.Println("duplicate rejected")
}
```

Every Go block in these docs is checked in CI: a block is either a complete
`package main` program that must compile, a program marked as runnable (this
one runs against PostgreSQL on every build), or an explicitly marked fragment
that must still parse as Go.

## Typed queries

Typed queries need generated code. You describe a table as a struct that embeds
`momo.Model`, run `momo generate`, and build queries from the generated
descriptors, so a misspelled column or a wrong value type fails at compile time:

```sh
momo generate
momo migrate diff init
momo migrate apply
```

The [quickstart example](../examples/quickstart/) shows the models, the
`momo.yaml` configuration, the generated packages and the first migration.
Then read:

- [Agent guide](ai-guide.md): the complete reference in one file, from tags to
  errors, with the pitfalls.
- [Type mapping](TYPE_MAPPING.md): the column type for each Go type.
- [Migrations](migrations.md): what `momo migrate` does and how to recover.
- [Relations](relations.md), [projections](projections.md) and
  [vector search](vectors.md).


# Source: ai-guide.md

# Momo guide for AI coding agents

Target: `github.com/azrtydxb/momo` v0.19.0. Read this file instead of the Momo <!-- x-release-please-version -->
source. Every identifier below was checked against v0.19.0. Where the guide says <!-- x-release-please-version -->
DON'T, the call either fails, silently does the wrong thing, or is a known bug.

Imports used throughout:

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
import (
	"github.com/azrtydxb/momo"                    // core: DB, Tx, Select, Insert, Update, Delete, errors
	"github.com/azrtydxb/momo/driver/pgxdriver"   // PostgreSQL driver (pgx v5)
	"github.com/azrtydxb/momo/vector"             // vector.Vector, HalfVector, SparseVector, Bits
	"github.com/azrtydxb/momo/types"              // types.UUID, Date, Numeric, JSON[T], TimeOfDay, Hstore, TSVector, TSQuery
	"yourmodule/models"                           // your structs
	"yourmodule/models/task"                      // GENERATED: one package per model (lowercase model name)
)
```

Deeper docs: [README](../README.md), [relations](relations.md),
[migrations](migrations.md), [vectors](vectors.md), [capabilities](capabilities.md),
[supported versions](supported-versions.md), [type mapping](TYPE_MAPPING.md),
[architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md), [examples](../examples/README.md).

## 1. Scope

- v0.19.0 supports PostgreSQL 16 and 17 with pgvector 0.8.x, through pgx v5; the other databases are in the status block below. <!-- x-release-please-version -->

Database status:

<!-- generated:status -->

<!-- Generated by go generate ./internal/gendocs from the code. Do not edit by hand. -->

A database is usable when a driver package for it exists under `driver/`:

- PostgreSQL: usable through `driver/pgxdriver` (vector builders: yes). Migrations: `migrate/postgres`, run by `momo migrate`.
- SQLite: usable through `driver/sqlitedriver` (needs cgo, not on Windows, vector builders: yes) and `driver/sqlitepure` (vector builders: no). Migrations: `migrate/sqlite`, run by `momo migrate`.
- MySQL and MariaDB: usable through `driver/mysqldriver` (vector storage and builders depend on the server version). Migrations: `migrate/mysql`, run by `momo migrate`.

<!-- /generated:status -->

- PostgreSQL is the reference database. Check the dialect columns of docs/capabilities.md before relying on a feature on another database. Keep `dialects:` at `[postgres]` for generated migrations. `momo migrate` exits 2 for a dialect it does not link; library migrations go through `migrate.NewEngine`.
- Go 1.26.10 or newer (the go.mod floor, which carries the standard-library security fixes). Pre-v1: no compatibility promise; pin the exact version.
- `diff` writes forward migrations only. `momo migrate rollback [--group]` runs a hand-written `.down.sql`, `momo migrate lint` reports risky operations, and `momo migrate rebase --onto <dir>` regenerates a branch's migrations on a target's.
- `momo generate --from-db DATABASE_URL` turns a live PostgreSQL, MySQL or MariaDB database into models and an init snapshot (see [migrations](migrations.md#7-adopting-an-existing-database) and [MySQL and MariaDB](mysql.md#models-from-a-database)). SQLite: write models by hand.
- Reciprocal-rank-fusion hybrid search is `momo.HybridSearch` (PostgreSQL,
  SQLite and MariaDB; `ErrUnsupported` on MySQL, see
  [vectors.md](vectors.md#hybrid-search)). Full-text search runs on PostgreSQL,
  SQLite and MySQL or MariaDB: declare it once on the model (the `search` tag or
  `c.FullText`) and search with `fts.Search`, `fts.Score` and `fts.Snippet`
  (see [fulltext.md](fulltext.md)); `types.TSVector`, `fts.TSMatch`,
  `fts.TSRankCD`, `fts.TSHeadline` and the query builders are PostgreSQL SQL. To
  weigh the signals yourself, combine a vector distance with a text rank in one
  score as shown in [fulltext.md](fulltext.md).

Details: [capabilities.md](capabilities.md). Example: [quickstart](../examples/quickstart/).

## 2. Install and tooling

<!-- x-release-please-start-version -->

```sh
go get github.com/azrtydxb/momo@v0.19.0                # adds the library to go.mod and writes go.sum
go install github.com/azrtydxb/momo/cmd/momo@v0.19.0   # the CLI: generate, migrate, import, viz, help
```

<!-- x-release-please-end -->

Run `go get` first in a fresh module: it produces `go.sum`, which `go run` and
the generated code's compilation need. `go install` puts `momo` in
`$(go env GOPATH)/bin`; make sure that is on `PATH`.

Layout of a project (the `models` package holds structs; `momo generate` writes
into it):

```text
go.mod
momo.yaml
models/models.go          # yours
models/momo_gen.go        # generated (MomoMeta for each model). Commit it.
models/task/momo_gen.go   # generated: columns and relations of Task. Commit it.
migrations/               # momo migrate diff writes here. Commit it.
```

Minimal `momo.yaml` (at the module root; the CLI finds it by walking up to `go.mod`):

```yaml
version: 1
packages:
  - ./models
dialects: [postgres]
migrate:
  dir:
    postgres: migrations
  url_env:
    postgres: DATABASE_URL
```

`naming:` is optional: `momo` (default: snake_case columns, plural snake_case
tables), `gorm`, `bun`, `ent`, `prisma`. Pick one and never change it: a change
renames columns. The `momo` preset keeps an initialism together, and a plural
`s` after it belongs to it: `RoleIDs` is `role_ids`, `URLs` is `urls`,
`HTTPServer` is `http_server`.

`naming: prisma` matches a database that Prisma created: the table is the model
name as written and quoted (`KbChunk`), the column is camelCase (`createdAt`,
`accountId`; an `ID` word at the end becomes `Id`, and a trailing `IDs` becomes
`Ids`, so `UserIDs` is `userIds`), and the constraint and index names are
`<Table>_pkey`, `<Table>_<col>_fkey`, `<Table>_<col>_key` (unique) and
`<Table>_<col>_idx`. Those names come out of the table and column names, so no
tag is needed for single-column keys and indexes.

Limits of the preset:

- A composite `@@index` or `@@unique` is named by Prisma from all its columns
  (`<Table>_<a>_<b>_idx`). Name such an index explicitly in `MomoConfig` or with
  an `index:`/`unique:` tag name.
- The implicit many-to-many table is named `_AToB` (model names in alphabetical
  order), but its `A` and `B` columns and its foreign key names are not
  reproduced. Declare that table with an explicit join model instead.
- A column name that does not follow the camelCase rule needs a `column:` tag.

Prisma maps `DateTime` to `timestamp(3)`, so add a `types:` section:

```yaml
naming: prisma
types:
  time.Time: timestamp(3)
```

`types:` overrides the default PostgreSQL column type of a Go type. Only
`time.Time` is supported, and the value must be `timestamp`, `timestamptz`,
`time` or `timetz` with an optional precision 0-6 and an optional
`with`/`without time zone` (anything else is refused, as it is written into
DDL). A `type:` tag on a field still wins. It applies when the first entry of
`dialects` is PostgreSQL (or `dialects` is empty); with SQLite first it is
ignored. Without it `time.Time` is `timestamp with time zone`.

Generate:

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
//go:generate momo generate
```

```sh
momo generate            # writes *_gen.go
momo generate --check    # CI: exit 1 and "stale: <path>" lines when stale; writes nothing
```

Rules:

- DO run `momo generate` after every change to a model struct or tag, before
  compiling code that uses the generated packages.
- DO commit generated files. DON'T edit `*_gen.go` and DON'T name your own
  files `*_gen.go` (the generator refuses to overwrite non-generated files).
- DO put `*_gen.go text eol=lf` in `.gitattributes` if anyone uses Windows, to
  keep checkouts byte-identical (`--check` already treats a CRLF copy as current).
- DON'T use `go run` of the CLI inside app code; the library (`momo`) never
  imports the generator.

Details: README "Configure and generate". Example: [quickstart](../examples/quickstart/).

## 3. Connecting

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
func openDB(ctx context.Context, url string) (*momo.DB, func(), error) {
	drv, err := pgxdriver.Open(ctx, url) // (ctx, string, ...Option) (momo.Driver, error)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, nil, err
	}
	db := momo.New(drv)
	return db, func() { _ = db.Close() }, nil
}
```

- One constructor shape for every driver package. `Open(ctx, dsn, opts...)`
  opens the database and returns a `momo.Driver` that owns it: `db.Close()`
  closes it. `New(handle, opts...)` wraps a pool or `*sql.DB` you opened
  (`pgxdriver.New(pool)`, `pgxdriver.NewSQL(db)`, `sqlitedriver.New(db)`,
  `sqlitepure.New(db)`, `mysqldriver.New(db)`), does not own it and never
  closes it: `db.Close()` returns nil and leaves it open. `New` refuses an
  option that tries to configure the open pool, with `ErrValidation`.
- SQLite settings are options: `sqlitedriver.WithConfig(cfg)`,
  `sqlitedriver.WithBusyTimeout`, `sqlitedriver.WithSynchronous`,
  `sqlitedriver.WithTxLock` and `sqlitedriver.WithMaxOpenConns`, and
  `sqlitepure.WithReadOnly`. The MySQL flavor is `mysqldriver.WithFlavor`
  (`dialect.FlavorMariaDB` for MariaDB; the default is MySQL).
- `*momo.DB` is safe for concurrent use; create one at startup and share it.
- DSN: `postgres://user:password@host:5432/dbname?sslmode=verify-full`. Use
  `sslmode=disable` for local development only. Momo adds no TLS options; pgx
  reads `sslmode`, `sslrootcert`, ... from the URL.
- Read the URL from the environment, never hard-code credentials.
- Pool sizing: Momo documents no recommendation and sets nothing. pgxpool
  options (for example `pool_max_conns=N` in the URL) apply. Each open `Tx`,
  `vecsearch.With` block, `Replace` and `CreateGraph` holds one connection for its
  whole duration.

Other constructors:

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
drv, err := pgxdriver.OpenSQL(ctx, url) // database/sql on the pgx stdlib driver; drv owns the *sql.DB
drv = pgxdriver.NewSQL(sqlDB)           // sqlDB must be backed by pgx stdlib; you own it; for an existing *sql.Tx see SQLTx, AdoptTx and UnwrapSQLTx in section Transactions
```

`database/sql` paths have no Batch or COPY path (relation loading falls back to
sequential statements; correct, just slower).

PgBouncer (transaction pooling):

- `pgxdriver.New` defaults to `pgx.QueryExecModeExec` (unnamed statements,
  server-side binding). That is PgBouncer-safe; set nothing.
- That mode sends no parameter types, so the driver converts what pgx cannot
  encode. `[]uuid.UUID` (github.com/google/uuid), `[]types.UUID` and any slice
  of a `[16]byte` type that implements `fmt.Stringer` bind to `id = ANY(?::uuid[])`
  (with or without the cast; a nil slice is NULL). A raw `[]byte` is `bytea`
  text and a `jsonb` column rejects it: pass the JSON as `json.RawMessage` or
  `string`, or use `types.JSON[T]`. The pgxdriver tests
  `TestUUIDSliceBindsToAnyArray` and `TestJSONBBinding` pin this.
- `pgxdriver.WithExecMode(m)` accepts `pgx.QueryExecModeCacheStatement`,
  `pgx.QueryExecModeCacheDescribe`, `pgx.QueryExecModeDescribeExec` (import
  `github.com/jackc/pgx/v5`; not tested through PgBouncer). The simple protocol is rejected
  with `ErrUnsupported` on every query. DON'T select it.
- With `pgxdriver.OpenSQL` add `default_query_exec_mode=exec` to the DSN, and
  with `pgxdriver.NewSQL` set `cfg.DefaultQueryExecMode = pgx.QueryExecModeExec`
  before `stdlib.OpenDB`; pgx defaults to `CacheStatement`, which is NOT
  PgBouncer-safe. The options of `OpenSQL` and `NewSQL` have no effect.
- DON'T run `momo migrate` through a transaction pooler (section 5).
- Set `search_path` per role or per transaction, not at connection startup.

Details: [capabilities.md](capabilities.md) "Getting connected",
[supported-versions.md](supported-versions.md) "PgBouncer".

## 4. Modeling

A model is a struct that embeds `momo.Model` BY VALUE. The tag on that embedded
field names the table. The tag grammar is `momo:"opt,opt:value,..."`; a value
cannot contain a comma. An unknown, duplicate or malformed option is a generator
diagnostic and nothing is written for that package.

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
type Account struct {
	momo.Model `momo:"table:accounts"`
	ID         int64      `momo:"pk,identity"`
	Email      string     `momo:"size:200,unique"`
	Plan       string     `momo:"size:20,default:'free',index"`
	Note       *string    `momo:"size:500"`                         // pointer = nullable
	Balance    int64      `momo:"default:0"`
	Version    int64      `momo:"version,default:0"`                // optimistic lock
	CreatedAt  time.Time  `momo:"column:created_at,created_at"`     // set by Momo on insert
	UpdatedAt  time.Time  `momo:"column:updated_at,updated_at"`     // set by Momo on update
	DeletedAt  *time.Time `momo:"column:deleted_at,soft_delete:timestamp"`
	Embedding  vector.Vector `momo:"dim:1536"`                      // pgvector column

	Posts []Post `momo:"has_many,fk:AccountID"`
}
```

Nullability and column rules:

- A non-pointer Go field is `NOT NULL`. A pointer (`*string`), a `sql.Null*`
  type, or the `nullable` tag makes the column nullable. `notnull` is redundant
  for non-pointers and a diagnostic on pointers.
- A nullable field generates `momo.NullColumn[T]` (has `SetNull()`); a
  non-nullable one generates `momo.Column[T]` (`SetNull()` does not compile).
  For a `*T` value that may be nil, `col.SetPtr(p)` writes NULL when `p` is nil
  and `*p` otherwise, and `col.EqPtr(p)` renders `IS NULL` when `p` is nil and
  `= $n` otherwise. Do not branch on nil by hand.
- A primary key must not be nullable.
- Scanning NULL into a non-pointer field is an error. Use pointers for nullable
  columns. The one exception is a `dbdefault` pointer, which is NOT NULL (see
  Database defaults).
- Go type to column type: see [TYPE_MAPPING.md](TYPE_MAPPING.md) (`int` is
  `bigint`, `string` is `text`, `string` with `size:N` is `varchar(N)`,
  `time.Time` is `timestamptz`, `types.UUID` is `uuid`, `types.JSON[T]` is
  `jsonb`). `uint64`, maps and unknown types have no mapping: add `type:<sql>`
  or a codec.
- JSON columns: `jsonop.Text`, `jsonop.Path`, `jsonop.Contains` and
  `jsonop.HasKey` (package `github.com/azrtydxb/momo/jsonop`) are typed
  operators over a `types.JSON[T]` column; the extractions are string
  expressions usable in `Where`, `OrderBy` and `Columns`.
  An extraction is NULL for a missing key and for JSON null alike, a SQL NULL
  column is tested with `IsNull` on the column, and the JSON literal null is
  matched by comparing the column with a `types.JSON` whose value is nil.
  `jsonop.HasKey` is true for a key whose value is JSON null. A numeric key in
  `jsonop.Text` or `jsonop.HasKey` is an object key; only `jsonop.Path`
  elements made of digits can be array indexes. SQLite renders `json_extract`
  and `json_type` (`jsonop.Contains` is `ErrUnsupported` there); MySQL renders
  its JSON functions.
- JSON type name: `jsonop.TypeOf(col)` is `jsonb_typeof` and gives one of
  `object`, `array`, `string`, `number`, `boolean` or `null` on every dialect
  (SQLite and MySQL names are mapped), SQL NULL for a SQL NULL column and the
  text `null` for the JSON literal null. `sqlfn.Greatest` and `sqlfn.Least`
  ignore NULL arguments on every dialect (MySQL and SQLite are rewritten, so
  each argument renders once per argument); `sqlfn.Floor` and `sqlfn.Ceil` take
  a float or a `types.Numeric` and return the same type, and `types.Numeric` is
  PostgreSQL only. Together they replace the raw SQL of a per-row setting read
  from JSON and floored, with a minimum of one: a `sqlfn.Case` that tests
  `jsonop.TypeOf` against `number` inside `sqlfn.Greatest`.
- JSON edits and scalars: `jsonop.Root(col)` reads a scalar stored at the
  root of the value (`col #>> '{}'`; cast it with `sqlfn.Cast` for a number).
  `jsonop.DeleteKey(expr, key)` is `expr - 'key'` (SQLite `json_remove`, MySQL
  `JSON_REMOVE`), so a snapshot keeps every future column and still drops the
  secret. `jsonop.Concat(a, b)` is the shallow `a || b` and
  `jsonop.Set(target, path, value)` is `jsonb_set` with a path built in SQL
  (`momo.ArrayOf(...)`). Both are PostgreSQL only and `ErrUnsupported`
  elsewhere, because `json_patch` and `JSON_MERGE_PATCH` merge recursively and
  drop nulls. `jsonop.DeleteKey`, `jsonop.Concat` and `jsonop.Set` need `jsonb` on PostgreSQL: the
  `-`, `||` and `jsonb_set` forms do not exist for `json`. Their results are
  JSON expressions that `jsonop.Text`, `jsonop.Path`, `jsonop.Root` and
  `jsonop.HasKey` accept again, typed as the first operand without a check, so
  a mismatch shows only when the row is scanned. A SQL NULL value in
  `jsonop.Set` makes the whole result NULL: wrap an optional value in
  `COALESCE`. `jsonb_build_object` and `to_jsonb` are variadic `"any"`: cast
  their bound arguments (`sqlfn.Cast`), as PostgreSQL cannot type a bare
  parameter there.
- Column names default to the naming preset (`CreatedAt` becomes `created_at`).
  Fields are exported only; a tag on an unexported field is a diagnostic. Skip a
  field with `momo:"-"`.

Tag reference (all lower case):

| Tag                                                                       | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `table:<name>` (on `momo.Model`)                                          | table name; always set it. Also `schema:<name>`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `autoincrement`, `without_rowid`, `strict` (on `momo.Model`)              | SQLite table options: `AUTOINCREMENT` on the one-column `INTEGER` key, `WITHOUT ROWID`, `STRICT`; refused on other dialects, on a field, and for `autoincrement` on another key. `--from-db` writes them and `CREATE TABLE` carries them; changing one later needs a custom migration, and removing one from a model is not detected                          |
| `pk`                                                                      | primary key; several `pk` fields make a composite key, declared in field order unless `Config.PrimaryKey` lists the fields in another order (a tag `belongs_to` target needs a single-column key)                                                                                                                                                             |
| `identity`, `identity:always`                                             | database-generated identity (`GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY`; `identity:always` is `GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY`, so a client-supplied value is refused by the database; not on MySQL)                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `serial`                                                                  | PostgreSQL `smallserial`/`serial`/`bigserial` id by Go int width (sequence owned by the column, `DEFAULT nextval`); omitted from inserts and read back with `RETURNING` like `identity`; excludes `identity` and `default`; refused on other dialects                                                                                                         |
| `column:<name>`                                                           | column name                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `size:<n>`                                                                | `varchar(n)`; strings only                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `precision:<p>`, `scale:<s>`                                              | numeric precision (float, decimal, or a string without `size` that carries a numeric); `scale` needs `precision`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `dim:<n>`                                                                 | vector dimension; optional on vector and halfvec (none: dimensionless column), required on sparsevec and bit, invalid elsewhere                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `embed_from:<a>\|<b>`                                                     | names the string source columns or fields (separated by `\|`) of the embedding of a `*vector.Vector` field. The generator adds a nullable `varchar(64)` hash column `<column>_hash` beside it, and `momo.StaleEmbeddings` and `momo.SyncEmbeddings` keep the embedding current (see Keeping embeddings in sync). Refused on MySQL                             |
| `default:<sql>`                                                           | column default, raw SQL (`default:now()`, `default:'free'`, `default:0`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `unique` / `unique:<name>`                                                | unique index (single column)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `index` / `index:<name>`                                                  | index; modifiers `sort:asc\|desc`, `nulls:first\|last`, `method:<m>` need `index` or `unique`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `idgen:<name>`                                                            | client-generated string id (`cuid`, `uuid`, `ulid` or a name registered with `WithIDGenerator`); filled on insert when the field is empty                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `dbdefault`                                                               | leave the column to the database default while the field holds its zero value (nil for a pointer field, which then writes false and 0 when set): a `Model`/`Models` insert omits it and reads the stored value back (see Database defaults)                                                                                                                   |
| `generated:<expr>`                                                        | stored generated column (`GENERATED ALWAYS AS (<expr>) STORED`); needs `read_only`, so Insert and Update never write it while Select and Where can use it; an insert does not read it back (select the row again, or use `ReturningAll` where the dialect has RETURNING). An expression with a comma goes through `Config.Generated`. `--from-db` writes both |
| `virtual`                                                                 | with `generated:<expr>` (or `Config.GeneratedVirtual`): the column is `VIRTUAL` (computed on read) instead of STORED. MySQL and SQLite only: a PostgreSQL target is refused (VIRTUAL needs PostgreSQL 18, momo supports 16 and 17). An error without `generated`. `--from-db` writes it for a VIRTUAL column                                                  |
| `version`                                                                 | optimistic-lock column (integer type)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `created_at[:unix\|unixmilli\|unixnano]`, `updated_at`                    | automatic timestamps; field type `time.Time`, `*time.Time`, `int64` or `*int64`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `soft_delete:timestamp\|unix\|bool`                                       | soft-delete marker; Go type `*time.Time`, `*int64` or `bool`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `read_only`, `create_only`, `immutable`                                   | write permissions: never written; written on insert only; never updated                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `sensitive`                                                               | excluded from the generated `ColumnByName` allowlist (use for secrets)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `type:<sql>`, `collate:<c>`, `check:<expr>`, `comment:<t>`, `enum:<name>` | raw column type, collation, check, comment, enum type                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `embedded`, `prefix:<p>`                                                  | flatten a named struct-typed field into this table (anonymous embedded structs flatten by themselves); `prefix` prepends to its column names                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `nullable`, `notnull`                                                     | explicit nullability (rarely needed)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

`MomoConfig` for what tags cannot express: composite or partial indexes, vector
indexes, checks, enums, views, triggers, policies. The generator reads this
method statically and never runs it; arguments are `&receiver.Field` pointers and
string literals only.

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
func (a *Account) MomoConfig(c *momo.Config) {
	c.Unique("accounts_email_plan_key", &a.Email, &a.Plan)
	c.Index("accounts_plan_live_idx", &a.Plan).Where("deleted_at IS NULL")
	c.Index("accounts_embedding_hnsw", &a.Embedding).
		Method("hnsw").
		Opclass(&a.Embedding, "vector_cosine_ops").
		With("m", "16").With("ef_construction", "64")
	c.Check("accounts_balance_nonneg", "balance >= 0")
}
```

An index name declared in `MomoConfig` must not collide with an auto-named
`<table>_<col>_idx` produced by an `index` tag (the `Plan` field above already
yields `accounts_plan_idx`); the generator refuses the duplicate.

Config methods: `Config.Index`, `Config.IndexExpr`, `Config.Unique`, `Config.ForeignKey`, `Config.Check`, `Config.CheckIn`, `Config.Enum`, `Config.Default`, `Config.Generated`,
`Config.Comment`, `Config.Collate`, `Config.IDGen`, `Config.FKName`, `Config.Exclude`, `Config.PrimaryKey`, `Config.PrimaryKeyDeferrable`, `Config.PrimaryKeyInitiallyDeferred`, `Config.History`, `Config.View`, `Config.Function`, `Config.Trigger`, `Config.Policy`, `Config.RLS`, `Config.Partition`,
`Config.PartitionOf`. Index chain: `IndexOpts.Unique()` (on `Config.Index` or `Config.IndexExpr`), `Where(pred)`, `Method(m)`, `IndexOpts.With(k, v)`,
`Opclass(field, op)`, `Desc(field)`, `Nulls(field, "first"|"last")`,
`Concurrently()` (`diff` writes the index as `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` in its own no-transaction migration).

A check that restricts a string field to a list of values is `Config.CheckIn`.
Write one value per line; the values are string literals. `CheckInOpts.Name`
names the constraint, which is `<table>_<column>_check` by default.

```go
package main

import "github.com/azrtydxb/momo"

func main() {}

type Ticket struct {
	momo.Model `momo:"table:tickets"`
	ID         int64 `momo:"pk,identity"`
	Kind       string
}

func (n *Ticket) MomoConfig(c *momo.Config) {
	c.CheckIn(&n.Kind,
		"archived",
		"draft",
		"published",
	)
}
```

`migrate diff` compares the list as a set, so the order of the values never
matters, and a change that adds a value is one `migrate.AlterCheckIn` change.
Two branches that add different values to the list merge as text and diff to one
migration that adds both. Removing a value is destructive: it needs
`--allow-destructive`, and rows that hold it must be backfilled first. See
[migrations](migrations.md#value-list-checks). An empty list, a repeated value,
a field that is not a string and an enum column are generator errors.

A unique expression index is `Config.IndexExpr` with `IndexOpts.Unique()`:
`c.IndexExpr("principal_email_key", "lower(email)").Unique()`. Each string is one
key: an expression, or the exact name of a column of the table, which is a plain
column key, so `c.IndexExpr("template_name_key", "company_id", "lower(name)").Unique()`
indexes `(company_id, lower(name))`. Add `Where("deleted_at IS NULL")` for a
partial one. It is an index, not a constraint, so it cannot be a foreign key
target. `generate --from-db` writes unique, mixed and partial expression
indexes back this way; an expression key with `DESC`, `NULLS` or an operator
class has no declaration.

A composite (multi-column) foreign key is declared in `MomoConfig`, not with a
tag: `c.ForeignKey("note_document_fk", []any{&n.CompanyID, &n.DocumentID},
"document", []string{"company_id", "id"}).OnDelete("CASCADE")`. The first list
holds `&receiver.Field` pointers, the table name and the referenced columns are
string literals, and `OnDelete`/`OnUpdate` take `CASCADE`, `RESTRICT`,
`SET NULL`, `SET DEFAULT` or `NO ACTION`. The referenced table must be the
table of a model, and the referenced columns, in any order, must be its primary
key, a unique constraint (`c.Unique`) or a non-partial unique index over plain
columns; otherwise the generator reports a diagnostic. The key is a plain
constraint: `diff` adds, replaces and drops it like a single-column key, and
`generate --from-db` writes it back. There is no `belongs_to` form for a
composite key; the relation still needs a single-column key.

An exclusion constraint (PostgreSQL) is declared with `c.Exclude(name, &m.A,
"=", &m.B, "&&")`: pairs of a field and an operator, so `&m.RoomID, "=", &m.During,
"&&"` forbids two rows of one room with overlapping `During` ranges. Chain
`.Using("gist")` (the default; `spgist`, `btree` and `hash` also work),
`.Deferrable()` or `.InitiallyDeferred()`. A GiST constraint over a scalar column
makes the generator add the `btree_gist` extension. It models plain columns only
(no `WHERE`, expression or operator class); the other dialects refuse it. See
[migrations](migrations.md#exclusion-constraints).

A unique constraint, a foreign key and a primary key can be `DEFERRABLE` on
PostgreSQL: `c.Unique(...).Deferrable()` or `.InitiallyDeferred()` (a unique
with any other option is an index, which cannot be deferred),
`c.ForeignKey(...).Deferrable()` or `.InitiallyDeferred()`, and
`c.PrimaryKeyDeferrable()` or `c.PrimaryKeyInitiallyDeferred()` (call one of
them once). The other dialects refuse them. A foreign key cannot reference a
deferrable primary key or unique constraint, because PostgreSQL refuses it:
the generator and `migrate.Diff` report an error that names the foreign key and the
key, so keep a key that other tables reference immediate. See
[migrations](migrations.md#deferrable-constraints).

A model keeps an audit history on PostgreSQL with `c.History()` (call it once;
the model needs a primary key and a table in the current schema). The generator
declares `<table>_history` (the model's columns plus `history_id`,
`history_operation`, `history_changed_at` and `history_changed_by`), the function
`<table>_history_fn` and the trigger `<table>_history_trg`, which records the new
row of an insert or update and the removed row of a delete, whoever makes the
change. Never declare those objects by hand next to `c.History()`: they are
ordinary schema objects, so `migrate diff` mirrors a column added, altered or
renamed on the model on the history table in the same plan (a column the model
drops stays there as nullable, so no audit data is lost; `--rename-table` and
`--rename-column` follow too), and `generate --from-db` writes `c.History()` for
a database whose history objects match exactly. A primary key change closes the
old key's timeline with a DELETE row, and an UPDATE that changes nothing records
nothing. Record the
actor with `momo.SetActor` on the `*momo.Tx` before the change (a
transaction-local setting; a change made without it records a NULL actor), and
read the versions with `momo.HistoryOf` (every version of a row) and
`momo.HistoryAsOf` (its state at a time, `momo.ErrNotFound` when the row did not
exist then); both take the primary key values after the handle, and accept a
`momo.TenantFilter(ctx, column)` after them to scope the read to a tenant.
SQLite, MySQL and MariaDB refuse it: a generator
diagnostic, and `momo.ErrUnsupported` from the three calls. See
[history](history.md).

Many-to-many needs `join:` with the same table on both models you declare it on
(the reverse side is optional, but if declared it must carry `join:` too):

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
type Document struct {
	momo.Model `momo:"table:documents"`
	ID         int64 `momo:"pk,identity"`
	Title      string
	Tags       []Tag `momo:"many2many,join:taggings"` // join table taggings(document_id, tag_id)
}

type Tag struct {
	momo.Model `momo:"table:tags"`
	ID         int64 `momo:"pk,identity"`
	Name       string
	Documents  []Document `momo:"many2many,join:taggings"` // optional reverse side, same join table
}
```

Relation tags (a relation is an exported field of struct, slice or pointer type;
it is not a column):

| Tag                      | Field type  | FK lives on | Notes                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------ | ----------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `belongs_to,fk:<Field>`  | `*Related`  | this struct | `fk` names the FK field on THIS struct; make it a pointer if the relation is optional                               |
| `has_one,fk:<Field>`     | `*Related`  | the target  | `fk` names the field on the TARGET                                                                                  |
| `has_many,fk:<Field>`    | `[]Related` | the target  | `fk` names the field on the TARGET                                                                                  |
| `many2many,join:<table>` | `[]Related` | join table  | set `join:` (same table) on every side you declare; the reverse side is optional; two key columns `<model>_<pkcol>` |

Extra relation options: `polytype:<column>` + `polyvalue:<value>` (both, on
`has_one`/`has_many` only: polymorphic), `on_delete:` / `on_update:`
(`cascade`, `restrict`, `set_null`, `set_default`, `no_action`; they affect only
the FK emitted for `belongs_to`), `no_constraint` (emit no FK), `fk_name:<name>` (constraint name when not `<table>_<col>_fkey`; or `Config.FKName(&m.FKField, name)`). `has_one` and
`has_many` create no FK constraint themselves; the `belongs_to` on the other
side does. Many-to-many join tables get a composite primary key plus two FKs with
`ON DELETE CASCADE`.

Generator diagnostics (nothing is written for the package until fixed): more
than one relation kind on a field; field type does not match the kind; target is
not a Momo model; `fk` missing or naming a missing field; `many2many` without
`join:`, or a declared reverse side without `join:`; `polytype` without `polyvalue` (or the
reverse), or on a kind other than `has_one`/`has_many`; `polytype` column not a
field of the target; many-to-many to the model's own type; `momo.Model` embedded
by pointer; a generic model; `size` on a non-string; `dim` on a non-vector;
sparsevec or bit field without `dim`; `scale` without `precision`; `notnull` on
a pointer; nullable primary key; unknown tag option; Go type with no SQL mapping.

What the generator emits per model `Task` (package `task`):

- `task.Table` (a `momo.TableRef`), one column variable per field (`task.ID`,
  `task.Title`), `task.As("t")` for aliased columns, `task.ColumnByName(name)`
  and `task.ColumnNames()` (an allowlist for user-supplied sort/filter names).
- One `momo.Relation[Parent, Child]` per relation field (`document.Comments`,
  `document.Author`).
- Vector fields become `momo.VectorColumn[vector.Vector]` (nullable:
  `NullVectorColumn`).
- `read_only` / `create_only` / `immutable` fields become permission-typed
  columns that have no `Column.Set` (or insert-only `Column.Set`).
- Package name = lowercase model name. It can collide with your local variable
  names (`task := ...` shadows the package). Name variables differently or
  alias the import.

### Client-generated ids

Databases that keep ids as text and generate them in the client (Prisma
`@default(cuid())`) have no column default to lean on. Declare the generator
on the field, with the tag or in `MomoConfig`:

```go
package main

import "github.com/azrtydxb/momo"

func main() {}

type Contact struct {
	momo.Model `momo:"table:contacts"`
	ID         string `momo:"pk,idgen:cuid"`
	Name       string
}

type Note struct {
	momo.Model `momo:"table:notes"`
	ID         string `momo:"pk"`
}

func (n *Note) MomoConfig(c *momo.Config) { c.IDGen(&n.ID, "ulid") }
```

- Built-in generators: `cuid` (25 characters in the layout Prisma writes, so old
  and new ids look alike), `uuid` (random, version 4, 36 characters) and `ulid`
  (26 characters, sortable by creation time). Register your own, or replace a
  built-in, with `momo.New(drv, momo.WithIDGenerator("short", fn))` and tag
  `idgen:short`. Names are lowercase; the `MomoConfig` form takes a string
  literal.
- The generator fires when an insert writes the field and it holds the Go zero
  value: `Model`, `Models`, `Upsert` and every chunk of a bulk insert. An id you
  assigned is kept. The generated id is stored in your struct (the model you
  passed, or the slice element), so read `m.ID` after `Exec` or `Rows`.
- The field must be a `string` kind (named string types and `*string` work). Any
  other type, a name given twice (tag and `MomoConfig`) or `identity`/`serial`
  on the same field is refused by the generator. A name that is neither built in
  nor registered fails the insert with `ErrValidation`.
- A column named in `Omit` always takes a fresh generated id, which is bound
  and written back like any other. `InsertQuery.Values` and `InsertQuery.ValuesRows` that leave the id
  out get one too. `SQL()` shows a generated id in the arguments but does not
  store it in the model.
- On an `OnConflict` upsert whose target is not the primary key, the row in the
  database may keep its own id. `Exec` then asks the database for the stored id
  and writes that into the model (a `DoUpdate` that hit an existing row gives
  that row's id). A model whose row `DoNothing` skipped keeps the id it had,
  usually empty. This needs `RETURNING`; without it (MySQL) the id is not
  written back for such statements. `Rows` never writes back there: read the id
  from the returned rows.
- When the id is written back up front (every statement except the conflict
  case above), it stays in your struct also when the insert fails. Retrying the
  same struct reuses the id, and so do all rows of a failed chunked insert. Clear
  the field to get a new one. In the conflict case the model is updated only
  after a successful statement.
- In the conflict case, rows are matched to models on the conflict-target
  columns (or on the generated id for `DoNothing` without a target), so those
  columns must read back exactly as you wrote them; `citext`, `char(n)` and
  `numeric` columns may not. A returned row that matches no model fails with
  `ErrValidation` and the write is rolled back; only a pinned `OnConn` handle,
  which cannot open a transaction, keeps it. If two models share a target
  value, the first one is matched. A non-primary-key generated column (such as a
  `public_id`) counts as a conflict case too, because the kept row has its own;
  the default `DO UPDATE` set of `Upsert` leaves such a column out, so a
  conflict never replaces the stored value, even one you assigned; to overwrite
  it, pass an explicit `DoUpdate` that sets it. A single-statement insert that
  reads ids back runs in its own transaction (or savepoint), so a mismatch rolls
  the write back, and the models are updated only after the whole insert has
  committed. Inside your own `Tx` that means after the savepoint is released,
  not after your outer commit: if you roll the outer transaction back, the
  models still hold the ids of rows that no longer exist.
- The generator is a client-side convenience, not a secret. A `cuid` is built
  from the time, a counter and a process fingerprint, so it is guessable: do not
  use it for tokens or anything that must be unpredictable. Use `uuid` (random,
  version 4) or your own generator for that.
- A generator that returns an empty id, panics, or is registered with a nil
  function fails the insert with `ErrValidation`. The `ulid` generator does the
  same in the unlikely case that it runs out of ids within one millisecond.
- The tag adds no database default: the column stays `text primary key`.

### Database defaults

`InsertQuery.Model` writes every writable column, so a column with
`DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()` or `DEFAULT now()` is overwritten by the Go zero
value. Tag the field `dbdefault` to leave it to the database instead:

```go
package main

import (
	"time"

	"github.com/azrtydxb/momo"
)

func main() {}

type Event struct {
	momo.Model `momo:"table:events"`
	ID         string    `momo:"pk,type:uuid,default:gen_random_uuid(),dbdefault"`
	Title      string
	OccurredAt time.Time `momo:"default:now(),dbdefault"`
}
```

- When the field holds its zero value (the Go zero value, a nil pointer, or a
  value whose `IsZero` method reports true, such as `time.Time{}`), `Model` and
  `Models` leave the column out of the INSERT, so the database default applies,
  and `Exec` reads the stored value back with `RETURNING` into the struct you
  passed (the slice element for `Models`) once the statement has committed. A
  non-zero value is written as given. A pointer to a zero value counts as set.
- `Models` with a mix of zero and set rows writes `DEFAULT` for the zero rows
  (PostgreSQL). SQLite cannot put `DEFAULT` in a multi-row VALUES
  list, so `Exec` and `Rows` split the rows into runs of consecutive rows that
  agree on which columns are unset and insert each run as its own statement, in
  order, in one transaction (`SQL` fails with `ErrUnsupported`, as it renders a
  single statement). `Unnest` and `Copy` have no per-row default, so they fail
  with `ErrUnsupported` for such a mix: insert the rows separately or give every
  row a value. A
  column that is zero in every row simply leaves the column list. `Copy` has
  no `RETURNING` to read the value back, so it refuses a zero dbdefault column
  with `ErrUnsupported`: set a value, or use `Models`.
- MySQL has no `RETURNING`, so a zero dbdefault column fails with
  `ErrUnsupported` there instead of leaving the struct stale: set the value, or
  leave it out with `Omit` and read it yourself. MariaDB and SQLite read it
  back with `RETURNING`.
- Your own `Returning` list turns the automatic read-back off; `Rows` returns
  the columns you named. A single `Model` that a conflict action skips
  (`DoNothing`) returns no row: `Exec` reports 0 rows affected and leaves the
  model as it was. A bulk `Models` insert that returns fewer rows than models
  (a conflict action, a trigger or a rule dropped some) is matched by key when
  it can be: the key is the conflict target, else the primary key, it must be
  written from the model (not omitted, identity or read-only) and must not be a
  `dbdefault` column that is zero in some row. The key is then added to the
  `RETURNING` list, the returned rows are written back by key and the other
  models stay untouched; the insert fails only when the conflict action is
  `DoNothing` and a skipped model still has a `dbdefault` column unread. When
  the rows cannot be matched by key the insert fails with `ErrUnsupported`
  ("returned N rows for M models"), rolls back and writes nothing back: give
  the columns a value, or use `Returning` and `Rows`. Inside a caller's `Tx`
  the rollback is to a savepoint, not the caller's transaction, which stays
  open. A pinned `OnConn` handle cannot roll back: it returns the same error,
  says the returned rows were stored, and writes nothing back. The
  conflict-target column of an insert that also uses an id generator cannot be
  a `dbdefault` column that is zero in some row (`ErrValidation`). The
  default `DO UPDATE` set of `Upsert` leaves a dbdefault column out when a row
  leaves it to the database, so a conflict keeps the stored value.
- The zero value means "use the default". On a plain `bool` or numeric field
  that means `false` and `0` can never be written explicitly through `Model`: a
  `dbdefault` field with `DEFAULT true` always stores true when it is `false`
  in Go, and `momo generate` warns about such a field. The same holds for an
  empty string and a zero time. To write `false` or `0`, make the field a
  pointer on a NOT NULL column (`Active *bool` with
  `` `momo:"default:true,dbdefault"` ``): a nil pointer takes the database
  default and is set to the stored value after the insert, a non-nil pointer is
  always written, `false` and `0` included. The column stays NOT NULL. A
  `sql.Null*` type or the `nullable` tag is refused by the generator, because
  nil would stop meaning NULL; write NULL with `InsertQuery.Values` and
  `SetNull`. `Omit` still wins: an omitted column is not written, and a Go-side
  default hook still fills it.
- `Update(...).Model(&m)` treats a nil `dbdefault` pointer as "not set": it
  leaves the column out of `SET`, so the column keeps its stored value (writing
  NULL would fail on the NOT NULL column). A pointer to `false` or `0` is
  written. If that leaves nothing to set, the update fails with the usual
  `ErrValidation` ("no columns to update"), unless the model has an
  `updated_at` column: then it is a touch that sets only that column. `Upsert`
  is unaffected: its default `DO UPDATE` set takes `EXCLUDED` values and
  already leaves out a `dbdefault` column that any row leaves to the database.
- The pointer type that `--from-db` generates and the `momo generate` warning
  cover only plain `bool` and number fields (`bool`, `int`..`int64`,
  `uint`..`uint64`, `float32`, `float64`). A named type, a type override from
  `introspect.types` or `introspect.columns`, a decimal or a string keeps the
  field as it is and gets neither the pointer nor the warning.
- `dbdefault` cannot be combined with `identity`, `serial`, `idgen`,
  `read_only`, `version`, `soft_delete`, `created_at` or `updated_at`; the
  generator reports it. It adds no database default (use `default:`), and
  `momo generate --from-db` writes it for NOT NULL PostgreSQL and SQLite columns whose
  default is computed (a function call, `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`, or a `nextval`
  sequence on a column that is not identity or serial); with
  `introspect.dbdefault: all` it writes it for every NOT NULL column that has a
  default, a constant one such as `DEFAULT 1` included; a `bool` or number
  column whose constant default is `true` or non-zero becomes a pointer field, so an
  explicit `false` or `0` is written. A hand-written model can
  put `dbdefault` on any NOT NULL column that has a database default. It never
  writes it for MySQL, which cannot read the value back.

### Model hooks

Give a model a method named `BeforeInsert`, `BeforeUpdate`, `BeforeDelete` or
`AfterLoad` with the exact signature `func(context.Context) error` and
`momo generate` wires it into `Meta.Hooks`; nothing else to register. A method
with a hook name and another signature fails the generator with a positioned
diagnostic, and a hook-named method on a projection is a diagnostic too
(projections run no hooks). The semantics (which builders run which hook, the
copy `BeforeInsert` receives, the error kind) are in the `HookSet`
documentation. DON'T edit `Meta.Hooks` in generated code.

### View models

A model that maps a database view embeds `momo.View` next to `momo.Model`:

```text
type ActiveUser struct {
	momo.Model `momo:"table:active_users"`
	momo.View
	ID int64 `momo:"pk"`
}
```

The generator sets `Meta.View`. Reads work as for any model; `Insert`,
`Upsert`, `Update`, `SoftDelete`, `BulkUpdate`, `Delete` and `Merge` return
`ErrValidation` naming the model, at run time (there is no compile-time
check). Declare the view itself with `c.View(schema.View{...})` in
`MomoConfig`. The schema the generator builds holds that view and no table for
the view model, so a migration never issues `CREATE TABLE` for it, and no
foreign key refers to it. `Materialized: true` declares a materialized view;
refresh it with `momo.RefreshMaterializedView(ctx, db, "name", false)` (a
name with a schema prefix, two parts joined by a dot, is split and quoted; the last argument adds
`CONCURRENTLY`, which needs a unique index in the view's `Indexes`). It is
PostgreSQL only and returns `ErrUnsupported` elsewhere.

### Generated servers

The `momo` binary has built-in `graphql`, `grpc` and `openapi` plugins, enabled
in the `plugins` section of `momo.yaml`. They generate servers over your models
with no authentication or authorization: wrap them. The `openapi` and `grpc`
plugins take `ops`, `read_only` and `on_error`; the OpenAPI document has a
`<Model>` output schema and a `<Model>Input` request schema. See
[capabilities](capabilities.md) for the options, error mapping and limits.

### Custom generator binary

The `momo` binary runs no custom plugins. To run your own `gen.Plugin`, write a
`main` that calls `cli.Main(plugins...)` from `github.com/azrtydxb/momo/cli`
and build it; it behaves as `momo` does and the plugins are enabled by name in
the `plugins` section of `momo.yaml`.

### Projections

A projection reads a column subset or aggregate into a non-table struct. Embed
`momo.Projection` by value; `momo generate` emits its `MomoMeta` into
`momo_gen.go` (every exported field, in declaration order; column name from the
naming rule or a `momo:"column:..."` tag). NEVER hand-write `MomoMeta` for a
projection. The `Columns(...)` list of the query must equal the struct field
order.

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
type Card struct {
	momo.Projection
	ID    int64
	Title string
	Score int64
}
```

Use it like this:

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
cards := momo.Select[models.Card](q).From(article.Table).
	Columns(article.ID, article.Title, article.Score).
	OrderBy(article.ID.Asc()).
	All(ctx)
```

When `From` is a plain generated table (`article.Table`) with a soft-delete
column (timestamp, unix or bool), the live-row filter is added automatically,
exactly as for a model; `WithDeleted()` and `OnlyDeleted()` work too. Do NOT add
`Where(<table>.DeletedAt.IsNull())` yourself. A `Join` does not change this:
the `From` table is filtered and joined tables are not. To alias use
`article.Table.As("a")`, which keeps the filter. The filter is NOT added when
`From` is a subquery or CTE, or a hand-built `momo.TableRef{Name:..., Alias:...}`
(it has no soft-delete column): filter those yourself.

If a package still has a hand-written projection `MomoMeta` from before the
generator emitted it, delete it (method and `Meta` variable); the generated one
redeclares it.

A projection cannot be inserted, updated or deleted (it embeds `Projection`, not
`Model`). Computed columns (a distance, `momo.CountAll()`) are valid entries in
`Columns`. The select list is positional and not aliased: the name you give a
computed column in `Columns` of the meta (for example `distance`) is only a label.

Tuple rows: for an aggregate, join or few-column read use `momo.Row1` to
`momo.Row10` instead of declaring a projection (no struct, no generated meta).
`Columns` is scanned positionally into the fields `C1` to `Cn`:

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
counts, err := momo.Select[momo.Row2[string, int64]](q).From(article.Table).
	Columns(article.Title, momo.CountAll()).GroupBy(article.Title).All(ctx)
// counts[i].C1 is the title, counts[i].C2 the count

// SUM is NULL over no rows: a pointer type parameter reads it as nil
total, err := momo.Select[momo.Row1[*int64]](q).From(article.Table).
	Columns(momo.Sum(article.Score)).One(ctx)
// total.C1 is nil when no article matches
```

A `Columns` count different from the arity is `ErrValidation` (no statement is
sent). Tuple rows are read-only projections: the same soft-delete rule as above
applies to the `From` table, and `After` needs a unique key in `OrderBy`.
NEVER hand-write a projection `Meta` for a tuple shape.

Examples: [projection-pagination](../examples/projection-pagination/),
[vector-search](../examples/vector-search/) (`Hit`).

Details: [TYPE_MAPPING.md](TYPE_MAPPING.md), [relations.md](relations.md) section 1.
Example: [relations](../examples/relations/models/models.go).

## 5. Migrations workflow

Flow: edit models, `momo generate`, `momo migrate diff <name>`, REVIEW the SQL,
commit, `momo migrate apply`.

```sh
momo generate
momo migrate diff add_plan              # offline; writes 3 files into migrations/
momo migrate diff init                  # first run on an empty dir: the initial schema
momo migrate plan                       # list pending (needs DB)
export DATABASE_URL='postgres://user:pass@host:5432/app?sslmode=verify-full'
momo migrate apply                      # [--to N] [--lock-wait 30s]
momo migrate status                     # applied | pending | dirty | mismatch | missing
momo migrate drift                      # live DB vs latest applied snapshot
```

- `diff` writes `<version>_<name>.up.sql`, `<version>_<name>.snapshot.json` and
  rewrites `momo.sum`. Commit all three. `diff` never overwrites; the name must
  match `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`; the version is a 14-digit UTC timestamp.
- `diff` compares models with the latest snapshot, never with the database.
  Prints `no changes` and writes nothing when equal.
- Never edit an applied migration file, even cosmetically: `apply` refuses on the
  changed checksum. For a cosmetic edit you accept: `momo migrate hash`, then
  `momo migrate rehash --version V --accept` (without `--accept` it only shows
  the two checksums); see [migrations.md](migrations.md) section 4. Prefer a new
  migration.
- Renames are never guessed: a rename looks like drop plus add and is refused.
  Say it explicitly: `--rename-column table.old=new`, `--rename-table old=new`.
- Destructive changes (`drop_table`, `drop_column`, `drop_enum`, a column type
  change) are refused without `--allow-destructive`. Type changes rewrite the
  table under `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` and fail on rows that do not cast.
- A `NOT NULL` column without a default on a table that exists in the snapshot is
  refused (`migrate.ErrStagedRequired`). Give it a `default:`, or stage it: `diff --stage`,
  apply, backfill, check `SELECT count(*) FROM t WHERE c IS NULL` is 0, then
  `diff --enforce-not-null`. The flag enforces every nullable column the model
  has as NOT NULL, not only staged ones; with NULLs left, `apply` fails (exit 3)
  and rolls back cleanly (not dirty): backfill and `apply` again.
- URL: `--url` (warns: visible in the process list; `--url -` reads stdin), else
  `migrate.url_env.postgres`, else `MOMO_DATABASE_URL`.
  Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 findings, 2 usage/config, 3 database/lock/execution error.
  An invalid migration name (`diff Bad-Name`) exits 3, not 2.
- Hand-written SQL migration: `momo migrate new --custom <name>` writes the up
  file (no `-- momo:generated` line), a snapshot copied from the latest one and
  the extended `momo.sum`; write the SQL, then `momo migrate hash` and
  `momo migrate validate`. The snapshot schema must equal its parent's. Directives (first lines):
  `-- momo:no-transaction`, `-- momo:split`, `-- momo:destructive`
  (informational). Unknown `-- momo:` directive is an error.
- Existing database: write models, `momo migrate diff init` (do not apply), then
  `momo migrate baseline --version <init version>`; the live schema must match
  the snapshot (extra objects: add globs to `migrate.exclude`). Example:
  [adopt-existing-schema](../examples/adopt-existing-schema/).
- The first migration with a vector column runs
  `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS "vector"`. pgvector must be installed on the server (image
  `pgvector/pgvector`), and the migration role must be allowed to create
  extensions, otherwise apply exits 3 naming the extension. An extension a
  superuser installs by hand goes in `migrate.external_extensions` in
  `momo.yaml`: no migration emits it and drift ignores it.

CI (every change):

<!-- x-release-please-start-version -->

```sh
go install github.com/azrtydxb/momo/cmd/momo@v0.19.0
momo generate --check                                   # generated code is current
momo migrate validate                                   # files vs momo.sum, version chain, forks, snapshots
momo migrate diff ci_probe | grep -qx 'no changes'      # models have a migration
```

<!-- x-release-please-end -->

The last line is derived from the code, not covered by a test: when models
changed, `diff` writes files (exit 0) and `grep` fails the job; discard the files
(`git checkout -- migrations && git clean -fd migrations`). There is no
`diff --check`. `validate` already verifies `momo.sum`; do not run
`momo migrate hash` in CI.

Production checklist:

1. `momo migrate validate` and `momo migrate plan` before apply; read the SQL.
2. One `apply` job per deploy, over a DIRECT connection (not PgBouncer in
   transaction mode: the lock is a session advisory lock).
3. Migrate first, then roll out code; every migration must be backward
   compatible with the running code (add, backfill, switch, drop later; a rename
   is add, copy, switch, drop).
4. Back up before any destructive, type-change or no-transaction migration.
5. Use a migration role without `statement_timeout`; `migrate.lock_timeout`
   defaults to 5 s and fails fast on a blocked DDL (safe to retry).
6. After: `momo migrate status` (exit 0) and `momo migrate drift`.
7. Failed transactional migration: nothing persists; fix and re-run. Failed
   no-transaction migration leaves partial state and a dirty row: finish or undo
   by hand in `psql`, then `momo migrate resolve --version V --applied` or
   `--rolled-back`. Full procedure: [migrations.md](migrations.md) section 4.

Known issues, as rules (each is a filed bug):

- For large tables declare `Concurrently()` on the index in `MomoConfig`: `diff`
  writes `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` in its own `-- momo:no-transaction`
  migration (a trailing `<name>_no_tx` file when the diff also has other DDL).
  Without it the index is a plain `CREATE INDEX` that blocks writes.
  A failed concurrent build leaves an INVALID index: `drift` reports it; drop it with
  `DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS`, then `resolve --rolled-back` and re-apply.
- `-- momo:no-transaction` applies to the WHOLE file: every statement loses
  atomicity and a mid-file failure leaves earlier statements committed (dirty).
  `diff` never mixes modes: it splits concurrent indexes, `ADD UNIQUE` and
  `VALIDATE CONSTRAINT` into a trailing no-transaction migration and keeps the
  transactional DDL in the first file. Keep hand-written no-transaction files
  to one statement.
- `-- momo:destructive` is informational: `diff` writes it, `apply` does not
  read it, so a hand-written `DROP` applies without confirmation. The only
  guard is `diff --allow-destructive`. Review every `.up.sql` like code.
- `diff` prints `risky:` hints for dropping an index, primary key, unique, check
  or foreign key and for adding `UNIQUE`/`CHECK`; these need no flag.
  `ADD CHECK` is emitted `NOT VALID` with a later `VALIDATE CONSTRAINT`, and
  `ADD UNIQUE` as `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` plus `USING INDEX`. Both
  can still fail on existing violating data. Hand-written changes are not flagged.
- NEVER edit an applied migration. `apply` and `status` refuse
  (`migrate.ErrChecksumMismatch`) and `momo migrate hash` alone does NOT fix it (the
  history row keeps the old checksum). Preferred: `git checkout -- <file>` and
  write a new migration. A cosmetic edit you accept: `hash`, then
  `momo migrate rehash --version V --accept`. Editing a still-pending migration
  is fine; then run `hash`. `hash` accepts every edit, so read its
  `changed:/added:/removed:` list first.
- `apply` refuses a forked snapshot chain (same error as `validate`) and a pending
  version older than the latest applied one (`migrate.ErrOutOfOrder`); both exit 1, as
  does a broken chain (`migrate.ErrChainInvalid`). Fix it with
  `momo migrate rebase --onto <target branch's migration directory>`, or by hand:
  delete the late migration's `.up.sql` and `.snapshot.json`, run
  `momo migrate diff <name>` to regenerate it with a new version, then
  `momo migrate hash` (a pending file needs no `rehash`); see [migrations.md](migrations.md) section 2. Still
  run `validate` in CI.
- `momo migrate rollback [--group]` runs the hand-written `.down.sql` of the last
  applied migration (or group); `diff` never writes one. Without a down file it
  exits 1 and runs nothing; prefer a new forward migration. `resolve --rolled-back`
  runs no SQL.
- There is no `--force-unlock` (an unknown flag, exit 2). The migration lock is a
  session advisory lock, freed when its holder disconnects. A stuck lock: find
  the session in `pg_stat_activity` and `pg_terminate_backend` it.
- `migrate.lock_timeout: 0s` and `statement_timeout: 0s` disable the timeouts
  (`SET ... = 0`); leave the key out for the defaults (5 s, untouched).
- `apply` with nothing pending writes nothing, not even the history table.
- `--url` is visible in the process list (momo warns): use `migrate.url_env`,
  `MOMO_DATABASE_URL` or `--url -`. URLs in history `error` text are redacted.
- `momo_migrations` lives in the first schema of `search_path`;
  `migrate.schemas[0]` must equal `current_schema()` or the engine errors.
- Dropped extensions and schemas are not dropped in the database.
- `AutoMigrate` (Go API) is additive only, writes no history; DON'T mix it with
  versioned migrations on one schema.

Details: [migrations.md](migrations.md). Examples:
[upgrade-database](../examples/upgrade-database/),
[custom-sql-migration](../examples/custom-sql-migration/),
[adopt-existing-schema](../examples/adopt-existing-schema/).

## 6. Queries cheat sheet

All builders take a `momo.Querier` (`*momo.DB` or `*momo.Tx`), so write helpers
that accept `momo.Querier` and call them inside or outside a transaction. Builders
are immutable values: every method returns a copy. Values are always bound
(`$1`...); identifiers come from generated columns. Errors from building (bad
column, wrong shape) surface at `SQL()` or at the terminal call.

Select:

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
tasks, err := momo.Select[models.Task](q).
	Where(task.Done.Eq(false), task.Priority.Ge(2)). // several predicates are ANDed
	OrderBy(task.Priority.Desc(), task.ID.Asc()).
	Limit(20).Offset(0).
	All(ctx) // []T; an empty result is a nil slice and nil error, never ErrNotFound

one, err := momo.Select[models.Task](q).Where(task.ID.Eq(id)).One(ctx)   // ErrNotFound / ErrTooManyRows
first, err := momo.Select[models.Task](q).OrderBy(task.ID.Asc()).First(ctx) // ErrNotFound when empty
n, err := momo.Select[models.Task](q).Where(task.Done.Eq(true)).Count(ctx)  // int64; ignores order and After
ok, err := momo.Select[models.Task](q).Where(task.Title.Eq("x")).Exists(ctx)
```

Predicates on columns:
`Eq Ne Lt Le Gt Ge In NotIn Between IsNull IsNotNull IsDistinctFrom IsNotDistinctFrom InQuery NotInQuery`
and `*Expr` variants;
combinators `momo.And`, `momo.Or`, `momo.Not`, `momo.Like`, `momo.ILike`,
`momo.ContainsLiteral`, `momo.Exists(subquery)`, `momo.NotExists`.
`momo.EscapeLike(s)` escapes user text for `Like`. Find NULLs with `IsNull()`;
`Eq(nil)` is not expressible.

Array columns (a PostgreSQL type). A `[]string` field is generated as `text[]`;
`[]int16`, `[]int32`, `[]int64`, `[]bool`, `[]float32`, `[]float64` and
`[]types.UUID` map to `smallint[]`, `integer[]`, `bigint[]`, `boolean[]`,
`real[]`, `double precision[]` and `uuid[]`. The predicates are generic functions over a typed column,
in the package `github.com/azrtydxb/momo/arrayop`:
`arrayop.Contains(col, vals...)` (`@>`), `arrayop.ContainedBy` (`<@`),
`arrayop.Overlaps` (`&&`) and `arrayop.AnyOf(scalarCol, vals...)`
