(`= ANY($n)`). Each binds the values as one array parameter, so the bind
count does not grow with the list. `arrayop.Overlaps` and `arrayop.AnyOf` with no values are
false. On other dialects they fail the build with
`ErrUnsupported`; use `In` there.
Array expressions: `momo.ArrayOf[T]` renders `ARRAY[e1, e2]` from
column, call or `momo.Value` elements (an empty list is `ErrValidation`), and
`momo.ArraySubquery[T]` renders `ARRAY(subquery)` for a one-column
`SelectQuery` or `momo.Union`. Both are `Expression[[]T]`, so they scan into
a `[]T` field and feed `arrayop` predicates; PostgreSQL only.

Range columns (a PostgreSQL type). A `types.Range[T]` field is generated as the
range type of its element: `int32` is `int4range`, `int64` is `int8range`,
`types.Numeric` is `numrange`, `types.Date` is `daterange`, `time.Time` is
`tstzrange` and `types.Timestamp` (a timestamp without a zone) is `tsrange`.
Build a value with `types.ClosedOpen(lower, upper)` (`[lower,upper)`),
`types.NewRange(types.Incl(a), types.NoBound[T]())` for any other shape, or
`types.EmptyRange[T]()`; a bound is a `types.Bound` with `Value`, `Inclusive` and
`Infinite`. The predicates are generic functions over the typed column, in the
package `github.com/azrtydxb/momo/rangeop`: `rangeop.Contains(col, element)`
(`@>`), `rangeop.ContainsRange`, `rangeop.ContainedBy` (`<@`),
`rangeop.Overlaps` (`&&`), `rangeop.Adjacent` (`-|-`), `rangeop.StrictlyLeft`
(`<<`), `rangeop.StrictlyRight` (`>>`), `rangeop.IsEmpty`,
`rangeop.LowerInfinite`, `rangeop.UpperInfinite`, and `rangeop.Lower` and
`rangeop.Upper`, which are scalar expressions (`rangeop.Lower(during).Ge(start)`).
Each binds its operand with a cast to the range or element type. PostgreSQL
stores the discrete ranges as `[lower,upper)`, so `(0,9]` reads back as
`[1,10)`. On other dialects the generator refuses the field and the builders fail
the build with `ErrUnsupported`. Multiranges are not mapped.

Searching with user input safely. `Like` and `ILike` always render
`ESCAPE '!'` on every dialect, matching `EscapeLike`. Wildcards (`%`, `_`) in
the pattern still work; only a `!` makes the next character literal, so a
hand-written literal `!` is written `!!`. Never concatenate raw user text into
a pattern. For a substring search use `momo.ContainsLiteral` with the column
and the user text; it is case-sensitive on PostgreSQL, while SQLite and MySQL
follow their own LIKE and collation rules. For a case-insensitive search on
PostgreSQL, pass `ILike` a pattern built as a percent sign, the user text run
through `momo.EscapeLike`, and another percent sign. A user typing `%` then
matches only a literal percent sign, never every row.

`ILike` works on every dialect, but it is emulated off PostgreSQL: SQLite,
MySQL and MariaDB render `LOWER(x) LIKE LOWER(?) ESCAPE '!'`. The results can
differ from PostgreSQL on non-ASCII text. SQLite folds ASCII letters only, so
`ILike` does not match `Ä` against `ä` there. MySQL and MariaDB fold with
`LOWER`, but the comparison follows the column collation, and the default
`_ai_ci` collations are also accent-insensitive (`a` matches `ä`), which
PostgreSQL `ILIKE` is not. Momo forces no collation. The `LOWER` around the
column means an index on the column is not used. On MySQL and MariaDB the
column must be a character type: on `BINARY`, `VARBINARY` and `BLOB` columns
`LOWER` does nothing and `LIKE` is case-sensitive, so `ILike` matches
case-sensitively there (momo adds no `CONVERT`). `momo.Not(momo.ILike(...))`
is NOT ILIKE.

A backslash is not an escape character. Without an ESCAPE clause PostgreSQL
and MySQL treat `\` as the LIKE escape; in momo a pattern such as `\%` means
a literal backslash followed by a wildcard. Replace hand-escaped patterns with
`momo.EscapeLike`, or write `!%` for a literal percent sign.

`In`, `NotIn` and tuple IN bind one parameter per value. A list over the
dialect bind limit (PostgreSQL 65535, MySQL 65535, SQLite 32766, or a lower
`WithMaxParams`) fails at build time with `ErrValidation`, not at the driver.
The check counts the binds rendered before the list; binds rendered after it
are left to the driver. Cap or chunk request-supplied lists yourself. An empty
`In` renders a constant false and an empty `NotIn` a constant true.

Two independent caps apply to a typed `In` or `NotIn` list. `WithMaxInList(n)`
limits the number of values per list and fails the build with
`ErrLimitExceeded`; it is for request-supplied lists. The bind limit above is
the database ceiling for the whole statement and fails with `ErrValidation`.
Both are checked at build time, the list cap first, so the stricter one wins.
`SelectQuery.MaxRows(n)` is the matching cap on results: `All` and `Pluck`
return `ErrLimitExceeded` instead of more than n rows, never a truncated slice.

Other builder methods: `Distinct`, `Join`, `LeftJoin`, `CrossJoin`,
`GroupBy`, `Having`, `ForUpdate` (with the options `"NOWAIT"` or
`"SKIP LOCKED"`), `ForShare`, `ForNoKeyUpdate` and `ForKeyShare` (PostgreSQL
only: `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` does not block foreign-key inserts on the locked
row, `FOR KEY SHARE` is the weakest lock; same options; MySQL and SQLite
return `ErrUnsupported`), `LockOf` (names the tables a lock covers, for
example `ForUpdate("SKIP LOCKED").LockOf("d")` on a joined job claim; the names must be
table or alias names, not CTEs), `SelectQuery.With`, `WithRecursive`, `Union` (a member with its own
`ORDER BY`, `LIMIT`, `OFFSET` or lock is parenthesised, a derived table on
SQLite), `SelectUnion[T]` (runs a union at the top level with an outer
`OrderBy`, `Limit` and `Offset`; `All`, `Rows`),
`FromSubquery`, `Each` (a context and a callback per row) and `Iter` (a
context; it returns `iter.Seq2[T, error]`). `Count` and `Exists` wrap the whole
statement, so they keep a lock clause and lock the rows they count. Aggregates: `momo.CountAll`,
`CountOf`, `CountDistinct`, `Sum`, `SumInt`, `SumNumeric`, `Avg`, `AvgNumeric`, `Min`, `Max`.

Pick the sum or average by the column type. `momo.Sum` keeps an `int64` or
`float64` column's own type. For an int16 or int32 column (a Prisma `Int` is
int4) use `momo.SumInt`, which takes int, int8, int16, int32 or int64 and returns an
`int64` on every dialect with no `sqlfn.Cast` (PostgreSQL gets
`CAST(SUM(x) AS bigint)`; a sum past int64 is an error). For an exact result use
`momo.SumNumeric` or `momo.AvgNumeric`, which return `types.Numeric` and take an
integer or `types.Numeric` column; SQLite cannot add a TEXT `types.Numeric`
column exactly, so `SumNumeric` over one and every `AvgNumeric` are
`ErrUnsupported` there. `momo.Avg` takes an integer, float or `types.Numeric`
column and returns `float64` (PostgreSQL gets `CAST(AVG(x) AS double precision)`).
On MySQL and MariaDB a value or sum beyond `DECIMAL(65,30)` (more than 35
integer digits) saturates or warns rather than erroring, and NaN and Infinity
cannot be stored in the TEXT column. Numeric results differ in trailing zeros
across dialects (MySQL and MariaDB always give 30 decimal places), so compare
them numerically, not as strings. The SQLite `ErrUnsupported` message names the
aggregate and points to `momo.Avg` (float64) or `momo.SumInt` (integers).
All of them are NULL over zero rows: read them into a pointer, as `Sum`.

An aggregate takes `Filter(p)` (`momo.Agg.Filter`, `agg.Call.Filter`) on every
dialect. PostgreSQL and SQLite render `agg(x) FILTER (WHERE p)`. MySQL and
MariaDB have no FILTER, so momo renders `agg(CASE WHEN p THEN x END)` and
`COUNT(CASE WHEN p THEN 1 END)` for `CountAll`, which gives the same result for
every aggregate that skips NULLs: `Sum`, `Avg`, `Min`, `Max`, `CountOf`,
`CountDistinct`, `agg.String`, and `agg.Func` over `count`, `sum`, `avg`, `min`,
`max` and the `std` and `var` family. It also works as a window function with
`Over`. A value that `p` binds appears once per argument of the call. An
aggregate that keeps NULLs (`agg.JSONB`, which is JSON_ARRAYAGG there, or any
other `agg.Func`) is `ErrUnsupported` on MySQL and MariaDB with a message that
names the reason, because the rewrite would add a NULL element per
filtered-out row; filter in `Where` or a subquery. `agg.Func` over a raw `*`
with `Filter` is `ErrUnsupported` there too; use `momo.CountAll().Filter(p)`.

Advisory locks (PostgreSQL), in the package
`github.com/azrtydxb/momo/advisory`: two functions and four options.
`advisory.Acquire(ctx, q, key, opts...)` takes a lock and returns whether it is
held, `advisory.Release(ctx, q, key, opts...)` releases a session lock. The key
is an int64 or a string; a string is hashed with `hashtext`, or with the 64-bit
`hashtextextended(key, seed)` when you pass `advisory.WithHash64(seed)` (seed 0
matches `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended(key, 0))` in existing SQL).
The options are `advisory.Xact()` (transaction-scoped, `q` is a `*Tx`),
`advisory.Shared()` (the reader half of a reader/writer pair), `advisory.Try()`
(return `false` instead of waiting) and `advisory.WithHash64(seed)`. Never store
a hashed key, it can change across PostgreSQL major versions. Other dialects
fail with `ErrUnsupported`.

A transaction-scoped lock, `advisory.Acquire(ctx, tx, key, advisory.Xact())`,
ends at commit or rollback and has no release. A `*DB` with `advisory.Xact()`
and a `*Tx` without it fail with `ErrValidation`: open a transaction first.

A session lock, `advisory.Acquire(ctx, db, key)` with `pg_advisory_lock` and
friends, needs a handle whose statements stay on one connection: `db.OnConn(pc)`
over a connection from `Pinner.Pin`. A pooled `*DB` fails with `ErrValidation`,
because the lock and the unlock could reach different connections. The lock
lasts until `advisory.Release` or until the connection closes, so release
before `pc.Release()` (or `Discard` the connection if the release fails).
`db.IsPinned()` reports whether a handle is pinned. On MySQL and MariaDB the
same session functions take `GET_LOCK`, `GET_LOCK(name, 0)` and `RELEASE_LOCK`
under the name `momo:advisory:<db>:<key>`, scoped to the current database as on
PostgreSQL (`<db>` is 8 hex digits of `sha256(DATABASE())`; a text key is `s:`
plus 32 hex digits of its sha256, and `advisory.WithHash64` has no effect);
`advisory.Xact()` and `advisory.Shared()` are `ErrUnsupported` there. After an
`advisory.Acquire` error `Discard` the pinned connection.

Shared locks: any number of sessions hold the shared lock of a key together;
none runs while another holds the exclusive lock of that key, and the exclusive
lock waits for every shared holder. `advisory.Acquire(ctx, tx, k,
advisory.Xact(), advisory.Shared(), advisory.WithHash64(52))` takes the lock
`pg_advisory_xact_lock_shared(hashtextextended(k, 52))` takes. A release without
`advisory.Shared()` does not release a shared lock; pass the same `advisory.Shared` and
`advisory.WithHash64` options to `advisory.Release` that the acquire used.

The 20 functions of the earlier API (`advisory.Lock`, `advisory.TryLock`,
`advisory.Unlock`, `advisory.XactLock`, `advisory.LockShared` and the other
fifteen, with their `...String` forms) and `advisory.Hash64` are deprecated
forwarders that run the same statements. New code uses `advisory.Acquire`,
`advisory.Release` and `advisory.WithHash64`.

Typed expressions (no `momo.SQL` needed). Computed values (`momo.Func` and, in the
package `github.com/azrtydxb/momo/sqlfn`, `sqlfn.Substr`, `sqlfn.Lower`,
`sqlfn.Upper`, `sqlfn.Length`, `sqlfn.Case`, `sqlfn.Add`/`sqlfn.Sub`/`sqlfn.Mul`,
`sqlfn.Cast`, `sqlfn.Concat`, `sqlfn.CoalesceExpr`, `sqlfn.Greatest`, `sqlfn.Least`,
`sqlfn.Floor`, `sqlfn.Ceil`) work in `Columns`, `GroupBy`, `OrderBy` and `SetExpr`, and carry
the comparisons of a column for `Where` and `Having`: `Eq`, `Ne`, `Lt`, `Le`,
`Gt`, `Ge`, `EqExpr` and the other `...Expr` forms, `In`, `NotIn`, `Between`,
`IsNull`, `IsNotNull`; plus `Asc` and `Desc`. An `.As` alias belongs in the
select list: `OrderBy` accepts it and orders by the alias name, `GroupBy`
rejects it with `ErrValidation`. A `sqlfn.Case` used in both the select list and `GroupBy`
must be built with `WhenExpr` and `ElseExpr` from literal or column expressions: bound
`When` and `Else` values get a different `$n` in each place, and PostgreSQL rejects the
mismatch. Otherwise group by position or alias in an outer query. Keyset pagination with `After` and a per-parent
`LoadPerParentLimit` also reject an alias order key with `ErrValidation`, because
an alias is not valid in WHERE or inside a window ORDER BY; order by the
expression itself there.

`NullsFirst` and `NullsLast` on any `Order` work on every dialect, with the exceptions below. MySQL and
MariaDB have no NULLS clause, so momo renders `(e IS NULL) DESC, e ASC` for
`NullsFirst` and `(e IS NULL) ASC, e ASC` for `NullsLast`, which orders exactly
as PostgreSQL does. The expression `e` is rendered twice, so a value it binds
appears twice among the arguments, in order. `After` over a nullable key is
`ErrUnsupported` on every dialect, so an emulated NULLS term never meets a
cursor over NULLs. The outer `OrderBy` of a `SelectUnion` with `NullsFirst` or
`NullsLast` is `ErrUnsupported` on MySQL and MariaDB. So is a window whose frame
is `Range` with an offset (`Preceding(n)` or `Following(n)`) and whose single
`OrderBy` item has a NULLS term: the emulation adds a second sort key and those
servers need exactly one (error 3587). Drop the NULLS term or use `Rows`. A `Distinct` select that
orders by an emulated expression missing from its select list can be rejected by
MySQL (error 3065, with `ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY`).

A predicate orders through `momo.OrderByPredicate(p)`, which has `Asc()` and
`Desc()` and renders `ORDER BY (p)`: `OrderBy(momo.OrderByPredicate(t.BuiltinKey.IsNull()).Asc(), t.Name.Asc())`
lists rows with a `builtin_key` first. False sorts before true, so `(col IS NULL) ASC` puts NULLs
last on every dialect. A predicate has no `Asc` method of its own, because `Predicate` is an interface.
`NullsFirst` and `NullsLast` on it work on every dialect. `After` over a
predicate key is `ErrValidation`, and so is a predicate in the outer `OrderBy` of a `SelectUnion`
(unqualified result columns only). `OrderByPredicate(nil)` is `ErrValidation`; an `agg` call's
`OrderBy` needs `.Asc()` or `.Desc()`.

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
// Alias a select-list item. As[T] is generic; Agg, sqlfn.Case and Func values also have .As(name).
// Column.As is the TABLE alias, so alias a column with momo.As[int64](col, "name").
n := momo.CountAll().As("n")                  // COUNT(*) AS "n"
inner := momo.Select[Pair](q).From(momo.TableRef{Name: "docs"}).
	Columns(doc.TenantID, n).GroupBy(doc.TenantID)
// Subquery in FROM: read the alias back with a typed reference.
momo.Select[Pair](q).From(momo.FromSubquery(inner, "s")).
	Columns(pairK, n.Ref("s")).Where(n.Ref("s").Gt(1))
// CTE, no positional column names needed:
momo.Select[Pair](q).With("s", inner).From(momo.CTE("s")).Columns(pairK, n.Ref("s"))

// Strings (package sqlfn): sqlfn.Substr(e, from, length), sqlfn.SubstrToEnd, sqlfn.SubstrExpr (positions as
// int32 expressions), sqlfn.Lower, sqlfn.Upper, sqlfn.Length. Substr positions are Go values rendered
// as literals, so the same expression works in SELECT and GROUP BY.
// sqlfn.NullIf renders its value as a literal, strings included: sqlfn.NullIf(doc.Title, "").
sqlfn.Substr(doc.Title, 1, 10)
// Filter and order on a computed value:
//   Where(sqlfn.Substr(doc.Title, 1, 3).Eq("abc"), sqlfn.Length(doc.Title).Ge(3))
//   OrderBy(sqlfn.Lower(doc.Title).Desc(), sqlfn.Add(doc.Hits, 0).Asc())
// COALESCE over expressions (Coalesce takes a bound fallback value instead):
sqlfn.CoalesceExpr(site.Name, site.LicenseID)          // coalesce(a, b, ...)
// CAST: T is the result type you choose, the SQL type name is validated
// (words, optional (n) or (n,m)); names are not portable (MySQL: signed).
sqlfn.Cast[int64](momo.Sum(usage.Answers), "bigint")
// Concat: (a || b) on PostgreSQL/SQLite, CONCAT(a, b) on MySQL; NULL in, NULL out.
sqlfn.Concat(sqlfn.Upper(doc.Title), momo.Value("-x"))
// Any other function: Func[T](name, args...). name is validated (identifier,
// optionally schema.qualified); an Expr arg renders inline, other values are bound.
// Plain values bound by Func or an aggregate are not masked in hook events, even
// beside a sensitive column; only comparison predicates mask their other operands.
momo.Func[string]("btrim", doc.Title)
// momo.Func is for scalar (per-row) functions and returns an Expression[T] with no aggregate modifiers.
// agg.Func is for aggregate functions and returns an agg.Call[T], which adds Distinct, OrderBy,
// WithinGroup, Filter and Over. A custom aggregate called through momo.Func has none of those.
// Aggregates with their own ORDER BY (agg.Call[T], package momo/agg); chain OrderBy, inside the call.
agg.String(label, ", ").OrderBy(label.Asc())        // string_agg / group_concat / GROUP_CONCAT
agg.Array[string](label).OrderBy(label.Asc())       // []string; ErrUnsupported on other dialects
agg.Array[string](label).Distinct().OrderBy(label.Asc()) // array_agg(DISTINCT ...); Distinct works on String, JSONB and agg.Func too
// Expand an array column of an earlier source (PostgreSQL): CROSS JOIN LATERAL unnest(q2.flags) AS fl (flag).
fl := momo.UnnestColumn(q2Flags).As("fl", "flag") // q2Flags is a Column[[]string]; read it with fl.Column()
// Ordered-set aggregates (PostgreSQL): WithinGroup is required.
agg.PercentileCont(0.5).WithinGroup(run.DurationMs.Asc())      // float64
agg.PercentileDisc[int64](0.9).WithinGroup(run.DurationMs.Asc())
// JSON: T is the Go type the result decodes into (types.JSON[T]). Keys and
// separators are literals and must not contain a backslash.
item := agg.BuildObject[Item](agg.Field("label", label), agg.Field("n", n))
sqlfn.CoalesceExpr(agg.JSONB[Item](item).OrderBy(label.Asc()), agg.EmptyJSONArray[Item]())
// current_schema(): PostgreSQL; MySQL maps to DATABASE(); SQLite is ErrUnsupported.
sqlfn.CurrentSchema()
// Division and NULLIF (integers divide as integers on PostgreSQL and SQLite, as DECIMAL on MySQL;
// guard a divisor with NullIf on every dialect, a zero divisor is an error in PostgreSQL and MySQL strict mode):
//   sqlfn.DivExpr[float64](final, sqlfn.NullIf[float64](max, 0)); sqlfn.Div[float64](final, 2)
// Row-value comparison, the keyset position check; both rows need 2+ elements of the same count:
//   Where(momo.Row(w.CreatedAt, w.ID).Lt(momo.Row(me.At, momo.Value(id)))); also Le, Gt, Ge
// CURRENT_DATE, and 'infinity' / '-infinity' timestamptz (PostgreSQL only; ErrUnsupported elsewhere):
//   timeop.CurrentDate(); timeop.Infinity(); timeop.NegInfinity()
// Inline literal for text that must match in SELECT and GROUP BY (a bound value gets a new $n each
// time, PostgreSQL 42803). Ints, floats, bool, string and time.Time. A string has ' doubled and is
// refused (ErrValidation) with a backslash or NUL; a time.Time must be exactly 00:00:00 UTC and
// renders as a date. Anything else, bind with Value:
//   key := sqlfn.CoalesceExpr[string](tag, momo.Lit("none"))
//   key := sqlfn.CoalesceExpr[int64](grp, momo.Lit(int64(0)))

// Dates and times, package github.com/azrtydxb/momo/timeop (PostgreSQL; SQLite and MySQL render equivalents). Fields and
// units are constants checked against an allowlist; anything else is ErrValidation.
timeop.Extract(timeop.ExtractEpoch, doc.CreatedAt)         // float64, also Year, Month, Day, Hour, Minute, Second, Quarter, Dow, ISODow, Doy
timeop.AtTimeZone(doc.CreatedAt, "Europe/Brussels")      // zone is a validated literal; ErrUnsupported on SQLite and MySQL
// Local-day buckets: timeop.Trunc(timeop.TruncDay, timeop.AtTimeZone(col, zone)); a bare timestamptz truncates in the session zone.
timeop.Trunc(timeop.TruncDay, doc.CreatedAt)           // Second..Year, weeks start on Monday
timeop.Now()                                             // also CurrentTimestamp(); the database clock, not WithClock; fixed at transaction start on PostgreSQL
timeop.ClockTimestamp()                                  // clock_timestamp(): real time at evaluation, for a lease or fence sampled after a row lock; SYSDATE(6) on MySQL
timeop.StatementTimestamp()                              // statement_timestamp(): start of the current statement; MySQL is ErrUnsupported
// Intervals are an operand of AddInterval/SubInterval, not an expression of their own.
timeop.SubInterval(timeop.Now(), timeop.IntervalOf(7, timeop.IntervalDay))              // literal count
timeop.AddInterval(doc.CreatedAt, timeop.IntervalOfExpr(momo.Value(int64(n)), timeop.IntervalHour)) // bound or column count
timeop.AddInterval(doc.CreatedAt, timeop.IntervalOf(1500, timeop.IntervalMillisecond))           // also IntervalMicrosecond; SQLite rounds to the nearest millisecond (1500us adds 2 ms)
timeop.AddDuration(doc.CreatedAt, 1500*time.Millisecond)                                         // a time.Duration as a literal interval, no rounding; also SubDuration
// Difference of two timestamps, read as seconds: a Span has no value of its own on MySQL and SQLite.
timeop.EpochSeconds(timeop.Sub(job.FinishedAt, job.StartedAt))                                   // float64 extract(epoch FROM a - b); TIMESTAMPDIFF on MySQL, julianday on SQLite
timeop.EpochSeconds(timeop.Age(a, b))                                                            // age(a, b), PostgreSQL only; ErrUnsupported elsewhere; its epoch counts a month as 30 days and a year as 365.25 days, use Sub for elapsed time
// Date arithmetic on a types.Date column; the results are typed, so no momo.Typed retyping is needed.
timeop.AddDays(appeal.RespondBy, 3)                                                              // types.Date: (d + n) on PostgreSQL, DATE(DATE_ADD) on MySQL, date(d, '+3 days') on SQLite; also AddDaysExpr(d, momo.Value(int32(n))); a column count must be int4 on PostgreSQL, momo.Typed[int32] over a bigint fails at run time
timeop.DaysBetween(appeal.RespondBy, momo.Value(today))                                          // int32 whole days, a - b: (a - b), DATEDIFF, julianday difference; negative when a is earlier
// appeal.RespondBy.LeExpr(timeop.AddDays(momo.Value(today), 3)) is respond_by <= today + 3. Infinity: PostgreSQL keeps infinity + n and refuses infinity - date; SQLite and MySQL fail the build with ErrValidation for a bound infinite date.

// JoinSQL composes raw fragments with their args (Prisma.join). The separator is a fixed
// literal from an allowlist: "," or " " (parts as written), " AND ", " OR ", "||", "+"
// (parts and the whole parenthesised; MySQL renders "||" as CONCAT). A part is any Expr, usually
// momo.SQL(...). An empty AND join is 1 = 1 and an empty OR join 1 = 0, like And and Or.
var conds []momo.Expr
conds = append(conds, momo.SQL("status = ?", status))
q.Where(momo.JoinSQL(" AND ", conds...))               // JoinTypedSQL[T] declares a result type

// CASE (sqlfn.Case); branches share the type T. Else/ElseExpr optional (NULL otherwise).
sqlfn.Case[string]().
	WhenExpr(node.Hostname.Excluded().Ne(""), node.Hostname.Excluded()).
	ElseExpr(node.Hostname)

// Arithmetic on numeric columns (sqlfn): Add, Sub, Mul (bound value) and AddExpr, SubExpr,
// MulExpr (expression). Numeric only; a string column does not compile. A types.Numeric
// column works too, on PostgreSQL only (ErrUnsupported on SQLite and MySQL, where it is TEXT).
node.Hits.SetExpr(sqlfn.Add(node.Hits, 5))                         // hits = (hits + $1)
node.Hits.SetExpr(sqlfn.AddExpr(node.Hits, node.Hits.Excluded()))  // upsert accumulate
```

An alias must be a plain identifier (letters, digits, `_`, `$`, not starting with a
digit, at most 63 bytes); anything else is `ErrValidation`. Reserved words are fine
because aliases are quoted.

- DO order every paginated or `First` query; without `OrderBy` row order is
  unspecified.
- `Each` and `Iter` stream rows and return `ErrUnsupported` when the query has
  `Preload`.
- `IndexedBy` is `ErrUnsupported` on PostgreSQL. Don't use it.

Keyset pagination (do not use `Offset` for deep pages):

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
var size int64 = 20 // Limit takes int64
q := momo.Select[models.Task](db).OrderBy(task.Priority.Desc()) // PK is appended as tie-breaker
if cur != nil {
	q = q.After(cur.Priority, cur.ID) // ONE value per effective ORDER BY key, PK included
}
page, err := q.Limit(size + 1).All(ctx) // fetch size+1 to learn whether another page exists
```

`After` needs `OrderBy`, a value count equal to the number of effective keys
(`ErrValidation` otherwise) and NON-nullable keys (`ErrUnsupported` otherwise).
For a projection (no PK in its metadata) list the unique key in `OrderBy`
yourself. A keyset order that is not total skips or repeats rows. Example:
[projection-pagination](../examples/projection-pagination/).

Insert:

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
t := models.Task{Title: "write guide"} // Priority 0, Done false, Note NULL
// Model writes EVERY column except identity, read_only and Omit()ted ones; zero values are written.
_, err := momo.Insert[models.Task](q).Model(&t).Exec(ctx)
// Values writes ONLY the named columns; the rest take the database default.
_, err = momo.Insert[models.Task](q).Values(task.Title.Set("x")).Exec(ctx)
// Many rows, one statement (chunked atomically under the 65535 bind limit):
_, err = momo.Insert[models.Task](q).Models(rows).Exec(ctx)
// Read database-generated values (identity, defaults) back:
rows2, err := momo.Insert[models.Task](q).Model(&t).Returning(task.ID).Rows(ctx)
if err != nil { return err }
defer func() { _ = rows2.Close() }()
for rows2.Next() { if err := rows2.ScanModel(&t); err != nil { return err } }
return rows2.Err()
```

- DO choose `Model` when the struct is the truth, `InsertQuery.Values` when "unset" must mean
  "database default". A zero `Priority` with `Model` is stored as 0, NOT as the
  column default.
- `Exec` does not fill the identity into your struct; use `Returning(...).Rows`.
  `ReturningAll()` returns every mapped column. `CreateGraph` reads identities
  back itself.
- A write that returns one row reads it with `One(ctx) (T, error)` on
  `InsertQuery`, `UpdateQuery` and `DeleteQuery`, instead of the `Rows` loop.
  Without a `Returning` list it returns every column. It returns `ErrNotFound`
  when no row came back (an `OnConflict(...).DoNothing()` insert, or a guarded
  update or delete that matched nothing) and `ErrTooManyRows` when more than
  one did. Without `WithImplicitTx` or an explicit transaction the statement has
  already changed every matched row: run `One` inside `db.Tx` and roll back on
  `ErrTooManyRows`. With `WithImplicitTx` it is rolled back for you.
  `InsertQuery.One` is for a single-row insert: a multi-row `Models` insert is
  `ErrValidation` (use `Rows`). `AfterLoad` runs before the write commits, so an
  `AfterLoad` error rolls the write back, unlike `SelectQuery.One`. MySQL returns
  `ErrUnsupported`; on MariaDB insert and a single-table delete have `RETURNING`,
  so `UpdateQuery.One` returns `ErrUnsupported` there (MariaDB has no
  `UPDATE ... RETURNING`), and so does a `DeleteQuery` with `Using` (MariaDB
  refuses `RETURNING` on a multi-table `DELETE`).
- A `ReadOnly` / `identity` / `serial` / auto-increment column is never written by
  `InsertQuery.Model`, and a non-zero value in its struct field is DROPPED SILENTLY: the
  database generates a new value. To keep the value (an import, a backfill, a receipt number
  held in a non-key `serial` column) name the column in `momo.InsertQuery.Explicit`:

  ```text
  _, err := momo.Insert[models.Receipt](q).Model(&r).Explicit(receipt.Seq).Exec(ctx)
  ```

  `Explicit` takes the columns to write with the struct value (or the `momo.InsertQuery.Values` /
  `momo.InsertQuery.ValuesRows` assignment), also for `Models`, chunked bulk inserts, `Unnest`, `Upsert` and `OnConflict`.
  PostgreSQL renders `OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE` for a `GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY` column
  only; serial and `BY DEFAULT` need no clause, and MySQL, MariaDB and SQLite write an ordinary
  column. A zero value in an `Explicit` column depends on the dialect: PostgreSQL and SQLite
  store 0 as written, while MySQL and MariaDB refuse it with `ErrValidation` (the server would
  generate a value instead of storing 0), checking every row before the first statement is sent;
  leave the column out of `Explicit` to get a generated value. A column that is not
  identity, serial or auto-increment, a column the model does not map, a column of another
  table, the same column in `momo.InsertQuery.Omit`, and `FromSelect` or `Copy` are
  `ErrValidation`. An explicit value does not advance the sequence on PostgreSQL: run
  `setval` yourself (Momo never does). MySQL, MariaDB and SQLite move past a larger explicit
  value on their own, so they need no `setval`. With `Upsert` or `OnConflict` the explicit
  column is written by the INSERT only: a serial or identity column that is not the conflict
  key is never updated on conflict, and `DoUpdate(SetExcluded(col))` for it is `ErrValidation`.

- `InsertQuery.Models([]T{})` (empty) is `ErrValidation`.

Update:

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
// Set writes exactly the given values, including 0, false, "" ; other columns untouched.
res, err := momo.Update[models.Task](q).
	Set(task.Priority.Set(0), task.Note.SetNull(), task.Title.SetExpr(momo.TypedSQL[string]("upper(title)"))).
	Where(task.ID.Eq(id)).
	Exec(ctx) // res.RowsAffected
// Atomic arithmetic (no read-modify-write race):
//   .Set(account.Balance.SetExpr(sqlfn.Add(account.Balance, delta)))
// (Sub, Mul, AddExpr with col.Excluded() in an upsert, Case, Substr: see section 6 "Typed expressions".)
// Other assignments: col.SetDefault(), col.SetExcluded() (upsert), nullCol.SetNull(),
// nullCol.SetPtr(p *T) (NULL when p is nil).

// Whole row from a struct (writes every writable column, zero values included):
cur, _ := momo.Select[models.Task](q).Where(task.ID.Eq(id)).One(ctx)
cur.Done = true
_, err = momo.Update[models.Task](q).Model(&cur).Exec(ctx)
```

- An `Update` or `Delete` without `Where` fails with `ErrUnfilteredMutation`
  unless you call `.AllRows()`. DON'T add `AllRows()` to silence it; add the
  filter.
- `UpdateQuery.Set` with zero rows matched is NOT an error; check `res.RowsAffected`.
- `UpdateQuery.Model(&m)` identifies the row by primary key. Without a version
  column a missing row is `ErrNotFound`. With a `version` column the statement
  is `WHERE pk = ? AND version = ?` and `SET version = version + 1`: a stale copy
  fails with `ErrOptimisticLock`, a missing row with `ErrNotFound`, and after
  success your struct's version field is advanced. Reload the row and retry on
  `ErrOptimisticLock`.
- Only `UpdateQuery.Model` checks and advances the version. A `UpdateQuery.Set`-based update,
  `Upsert` and relation helpers do NOT. DON'T `Column.Set` the version, pk (see
  `AllowKeyChange` below), soft-delete, created_at or updated_at column directly (`ErrValidation`); writing a
  `read_only`, `immutable` (on update) or identity column is `ErrValidation`.
  `Rows` is not supported on a versioned `Model` update; use `Exec`.
- To rename a primary key, add `.AllowKeyChange()` to an update that assigns the key
  with `UpdateQuery.Set` and find the row by its old key in `UpdateQuery.Where`.
  Without it a key assignment is `ErrValidation`. Every key column of a composite
  key may be set. A key held by another row is `ErrUniqueViolation`; foreign keys
  declared `ON UPDATE CASCADE` follow the new key (SQLite needs foreign keys on,
  which `sqlitedriver` does by default). Read the row back by the NEW key.
  `Returning` yields the new key on PostgreSQL and SQLite; MySQL and MariaDB have
  no `UPDATE ... RETURNING` (`ErrUnsupported`), so select by the new key instead.
  `UpdateQuery.Model`, `BulkUpdate`, the `OnUpdate` field hook and an identity key
  still refuse a key assignment, and `AllowKeyChange` on a `BulkUpdate` is
  `ErrValidation`.
- `updated_at` is set automatically on `Update` (Set or Model), not on raw SQL
  and not on relation helpers.
- An `Update` with no assignment is a touch when the model has an `updated_at`
  column: it sets only that column and keeps every guard (`ErrUnfilteredMutation`
  without `Where` or `AllRows`). Without a writable `updated_at` column it still
  fails with `ErrValidation` ("no columns to update").
- The conflict branch of a `DoUpdate` always sets `updated_at` to the statement
  clock, as a bound value (not `EXCLUDED`), for `Upsert` and for a plain `Insert`
  with `OnConflict`; `DoNothing` does not. It is independent of the INSERT:
  `Omit` of `updated_at` and a `FromSelect` without that column affect only the
  insert branch, and an `Upsert` with an empty default set renders a touch-only
  `SET updated_at = <clock>`. A plain `Insert` with `DoUpdate()` and no
  assignment stays an error.
- DON'T assign `updated_at` inside `DoUpdate` (a value or `SetExcluded`): it is
  refused with the same `ErrValidation` ("cannot be set directly") as on
  `Update`.

Delete and soft delete:

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
_, err := momo.Delete[models.Task](q).Where(task.ID.Eq(id)).Exec(ctx)   // hard delete
_, err = momo.SoftDelete[models.Task](q).Where(task.ID.Eq(id)).Exec(ctx) // stamps the soft_delete column
_, err = momo.ForceDelete[models.Task](q).Where(task.ID.Eq(id)).Exec(ctx) // hard delete on a soft-delete model

live, _ := momo.Select[models.Task](q).All(ctx)                  // soft-deleted rows hidden by default
all, _ := momo.Select[models.Task](q).WithDeleted().All(ctx)
dead, _ := momo.Select[models.Task](q).OnlyDeleted().All(ctx)
```

- On a model with a soft-delete column plain `Delete` is refused with
  `ErrValidation`. Use `SoftDelete` or `ForceDelete`.
- The soft-delete filter applies automatically to `Select`, `Count`, relation
  loads and `Has`/`HasNo` of a model. It does NOT apply to raw SQL (`momo.SQL`,
  `momo.Exec`, `momo.QueryScalars`), or to a projection whose `From` is a subquery or
  a hand-built `TableRef` (see "Projections" in section 4): add
  `deleted_at IS NULL` / `<table>.DeletedAt.IsNull()` yourself. A projection
  read `From` a generated table (also with joins) is filtered automatically.
- A soft-deleted row still occupies its unique keys. `FindOrCreate` does not
  treat it as found: with a unique constraint that covers deleted rows the
  insert conflicts and it returns `ErrUniqueViolation` (it never returns or
  restores the deleted row). A partial unique index would release the key, but
  `FindOrCreate` cannot target one (its `ON CONFLICT (key)` has no predicate;
  use `Insert` + `OnConflict(key).Where(...)`). Use partial unique indexes
  (`Where("deleted_at IS NULL")`) if
  keys must be reusable.
- `DeleteQuery.Model(&m)` deletes by primary key (`ErrNotFound` if missing).

Upsert (PostgreSQL `ON CONFLICT`):

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
// Conflict target = primary key; DO UPDATE assigns every writable column from EXCLUDED.
_, err := momo.Upsert[models.Task](q).Model(&t).Exec(ctx)
// Any unique key, explicit behavior:
_, err = momo.Insert[models.Task](q).Model(&t).
	OnConflict(task.Title).               // needs a UNIQUE constraint/index on exactly these columns
	DoUpdate(task.Priority.SetExcluded()).
	Exec(ctx)
_, err = momo.Insert[models.Task](q).Model(&t).OnConflict(task.Title).DoNothing().Exec(ctx)
err = momo.UpsertByPK(ctx, q, &t) // one-call form of Upsert(q).Model(m); reads generated columns back
// Conditional upsert (lease/lock): update only when the condition holds.
res, err := momo.Insert[models.Lock](q).
	Values(lock.Name.Set("n"), lock.Holder.Set(me), lock.Until.Set(until)).
	OnConflict(lock.Name).
	// .Where(targetPreds...) here names a partial unique index as the target
	DoUpdate(lock.Holder.SetExcluded(), lock.Until.SetExcluded()).
	Where(momo.Or(lock.Until.Le(now), lock.Holder.Eq(me))). // columns = existing row
	Exec(ctx)                                               // res.RowsAffected == 1: you hold it; 0: refused
// Compare with the proposed row: lock.Until.LtExpr(lock.Until.Excluded())
```

Insert from a SELECT (`INSERT ... SELECT`), including a FROM-less select guarded by
`WHERE NOT EXISTS`, as one atomic statement:

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
// INSERT INTO meters (product, id, kind, ...) SELECT $1, $2, 'distinct', ...
//   WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM meters WHERE product = $7 AND legacy)
//   ON CONFLICT (product, id) DO NOTHING
row := momo.SelectExprs(momo.Value(product), momo.Value(id), momo.Value("distinct"), momo.Value(now)).
	Where(momo.NotExists(
		momo.SelectExprs(momo.TypedSQL[int]("1")).From(meterTable). // constant 1, not a bound value
			Where(meter.Product.Eq(product), meter.Legacy.Eq(true))))
res, err := momo.Insert[models.Meter](q).
	FromSelect(row, meter.Product, meter.ID, meter.Kind, meter.CreatedAt). // explicit typed target columns
	OnConflict(meter.Product, meter.ID).DoNothing().
	Exec(ctx) // res.RowsAffected: 1 inserted, 0 skipped
```

- `FromSelect` takes any `Subquery` (the first argument) plus the typed target columns:
  `SelectExprs` (a FROM-less or single-source select of expressions, with `From`,
  `Where`, `Join`/`LeftJoin`/`CrossJoin`, `GroupBy`, `Having` and `OrderBy`; the clauses
  work like those of `Select[T]`, and a join, `GroupBy` or `Having` needs a `From`) or a `Select[T]` query. The select list must have as many columns as the
  target columns (`ErrValidation` otherwise; a `SubquerySQL` is checked by the
  database). `FromSelect` runs no model hooks.
- The soft-delete filter on a `SelectExprs` source (including inside `NotExists`) is
  added only when `From` gets a `TableRef` that carries the soft-delete marker.
  Generated `article.Table` refs do; a hand-built `TableRef{Name: ...}` does not and then
  counts soft-deleted rows, so set its `SoftDelete` and `SoftDeleteKind`.
- Only the listed columns are written. Nothing is injected: no automatic
  created_at/updated_at, no Go-side defaults, no field validators. List those columns
  and select their values. Identity, serial, read-only and non-writable columns, unmapped or
  repeated columns, and mixing with `Model`/`InsertQuery.Values`/`Omit` are `ErrValidation`.
- Composes with `OnConflict` (`DoNothing`, `DoUpdate`, both `Where`s), `Returning`,
  `ReturningAll`, `Rows` and `Upsert[T]` (default DO UPDATE set = the listed
  columns). Placeholders number across the select first, then ON CONFLICT (`$n` on
  PostgreSQL, `?` on SQLite/MySQL). For the constant in `EXISTS (SELECT 1 ...)` use
  `momo.TypedSQL` with the SQL text `1`, as in the example: PostgreSQL cannot infer
  the type of a bound `Value` there.
- MySQL has no `ON CONFLICT` (`ErrUnsupported`) but a plain `FromSelect` works; a FROM-less select with a
  `WHERE` renders `FROM DUAL`.
- MySQL and MariaDB upsert with `ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE`, which cannot name a key,
  so the conflict target must be a unique key and no other unique key may be able
  to conflict. The one relaxation: every other unique key is made only of
  auto-increment columns the insert leaves out, e.g. an auto-increment primary
  key plus `UNIQUE(email)`, upserting on `email` with a zero identity. Anything
  else (the primary key as target next to another unique key, a second ordinary
  unique key, an explicit `InsertQuery.Values` key, a model without a schema) is
  `ErrUnsupported` and the message says which key is the problem.

- Upsert never overwrites pk, version, soft-delete or created_at columns, and does
  not advance or check the version (no optimistic-lock detection).
- `InsertQuery.Where` is the DO UPDATE condition: valid only after `DoUpdate` or on
  `Upsert[T]` (keeps its default set); after `DoNothing` or with no conflict clause it
  is `ErrValidation`. Columns render qualified by the table name (existing row);
  `col.Excluded()` is `EXCLUDED.col`, used with `LtExpr`/`LeExpr`/`EqExpr`. A false
  condition affects 0 rows and, with `Returning`, returns no row.
- `OnConflict(cols...).Where(preds...)` renders `ON CONFLICT (cols) WHERE ...` for a
  partial unique index (unqualified columns); PostgreSQL rejects the statement
  without it. It needs target columns (`ErrValidation` otherwise). Multiple `Where`
  calls AND. MySQL: both are `ErrUnsupported`. `Excluded()` in the target
  predicate is `ErrValidation` (use it in the `DoUpdate` `Where`). On SQLite the
  target predicate renders bool, integer, finite float and string values inline
  (`"live" = 1`), because SQLite matches the expression, so write the same literal in the index; a value
  that cannot be inlined (time, bytes, pointer, NULL, NaN, a string with a NUL
  byte) is `ErrValidation`, and a type with `Value()` is inlined as that value.
  This is golden-tested and run against a real SQLite partial unique index
  (write the index as `WHERE live = 1`). Write the literals in the index exactly as Momo renders them: integers as `2`, floats in plain decimal with `.0` for whole numbers (`2.0`) for magnitudes from 1e-6 up to 1e21, and exponent form (`1e-07`, `1e+21`) outside that range; otherwise use `momo.SQL`. The values appear in the SQL text, so they show up in
  logs and traces.
- Mixing zero and non-zero identity values in one `Models` upsert is `ErrValidation`.
  Explicit identity or serial values do not advance the sequence: `setval` it yourself.
  A `FromSelect` into a serial table cannot supply ids at all (`ErrValidation`).

Joined and CTE-prefixed writes:

- `UpdateQuery.From(src)` renders `UPDATE t SET ... FROM src WHERE ...` and `DeleteQuery.Using(src)`
  renders `DELETE FROM t USING src WHERE ...`. `src` is a table, aliased table, `momo.CTE(name)`
  or `momo.FromSubquery(q, alias)`, as in a join; reference its columns with `momo.ColumnOf` or the
  model's columns, join it to the target in `Where`, and assign from it with `col.SetExpr(srcCol)`.
  The soft-delete filter and interceptors do not apply to `src`: add that predicate to `Where`.
  MySQL and MariaDB render the multi-table forms (`UPDATE t, src SET t.col = ...`,
  `DELETE t FROM t, src WHERE ...`); SQLite has `UPDATE ... FROM` (3.33 or later) and renders
  `Using` as `DELETE FROM t WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM src WHERE ...)`, so `Returning` lists
  columns of the target only there (a source column is `ErrUnsupported`).
- With `From` or `Using` the unfiltered-mutation guard is stricter: at least one `Where` predicate
  must reference a column of the target table, otherwise the statement joins every target row to
  the source and fails with `ErrUnfilteredMutation` unless `AllRows()` confirms it. A condition
  only on the source, or a raw `momo.SQL` fragment, does not count. An `Or` counts only when every
  branch references the target (one branch off the target can be true on its own, which touches
  every target row); an `And` counts when any term does. `momo.Not` swaps the rules (a negated `And` needs every term on the target, a negated `Or` any term), and `momo.JoinSQL` with `AND` or `OR` follows the same rules as `And` and `Or`. The guard checks that `Where` references the target, not that it restricts it: a constant-true predicate such as `t.id = t.id` passes. `From` cannot be combined with
  `BulkUpdate` (`ErrValidation`), and `RETURNING` with `From` works on PostgreSQL and SQLite only.
- `From` and `Using` take more than one source (`From(momo.CTE("due"), otherTable)`), rendered as a
  comma list. With two or more sources the guard applies the same rule to each source: a source
  that no `Where` predicate references is cross-joined, and the statement is `ErrUnfilteredMutation`
  unless `AllRows()` confirms it. One source is checked against the target only.
- `Returning` accepts columns of a `From` or `Using` source or CTE (`momo.ColumnOf`, or a table's
  descriptors under its alias). On PostgreSQL a statement with a source renders its whole
  RETURNING list qualified, so a column the source shares with the target is not ambiguous. Read
  such a list with `momo.ScanUpdate` or `momo.ScanDelete`, which scan into a
  plain struct, projection or tuple row by result column name (`s.url` is `url`; two returned
  columns with the same name are `ErrValidation`). `Rows` and `One` refuse a source column
  (`ErrValidation`), since the model has no field for it. SQLite's RETURNING reads the modified
  table only, so a source column there is `ErrUnsupported`.
- `UpdateQuery.With` and `UpdateQuery.WithRecursive` exist on `UpdateQuery`, `DeleteQuery` and `InsertQuery`, with the
  `SelectQuery` signature. PostgreSQL and SQLite render the WITH before the statement; MySQL
  accepts it before UPDATE and DELETE only (`ErrUnsupported` before INSERT), and MariaDB refuses it
  there too (`ErrUnsupported`, not verified). A WITH on a bulk insert that would split into chunks
  at the parameter limit is `ErrValidation`, and a `UpdateQuery.With` combined with `BulkUpdate` is
  `ErrValidation`.
- `InsertQuery`, `UpdateQuery` and `DeleteQuery` with `Returning` are `Subquery` values, usable as
  the body of `SelectQuery.With` on any statement: a select with `.With("x", ins).From(momo.CTE("x"))` renders
  `WITH x AS (INSERT ... RETURNING ...) SELECT ... FROM x`. PostgreSQL has data-modifying
  CTEs; SQLite and MySQL return `ErrUnsupported`. A DML body needs `Returning` only when the outer
  statement reads the CTE; a body that nothing reads (`WITH d AS (DELETE ...) INSERT ...`) builds
  without it, and PostgreSQL reports the error if it is read. A DML body renders with the handle's interceptors
  (with a background context) but runs no model hooks and no `beforeWrite` check; the outer
  statement's `Exec` or `All` is what executes it. An INSERT body is never chunked: one that
  binds more parameters than the dialect allows fails with `ErrLimitExceeded`.

Bulk and set-based writes:

- `InsertQuery[T].Copy` streams models through the driver COPY path. It returns `ErrUnsupported` on SQLite and MySQL and through `pgxdriver.NewSQL` (the driver must offer a COPY path). It runs the insert interceptors (deny only, a predicate they add is ignored) and the `BeforeInsert` hook over a copy of the models, validates fields like `Models`, and counts as a write for `NewUnitOfWork`. It skips `OnConflict`, `Returning` and chunking, and it cannot be combined with `Model`, `Models`, `InsertQuery.Values`, `FromSelect`, `OnConflict` or `Upsert` (`ErrValidation`). On a `*DB` with `WithImplicitTx` it runs in its own transaction, so `WithTxSetup` applies; on a pinned `OnConn` handle with `WithTxSetup` it fails closed with `ErrUnsupported`.
- `InsertQuery[T].Unnest()` (the method, not the package-level FROM source `momo.Unnest`) renders a `Model` or `Models` insert as `INSERT ... SELECT * FROM unnest($1::bigint[], $2::text[])`: one array parameter per written column, one statement. The bind count does not depend on the row count, so it bypasses `MaxParams` and `WithMaxParams` and never chunks (and is not split into a transaction of several statements). Other dialects return `ErrUnsupported`. `InsertQuery.Values`, `InsertQuery.ValuesRows` and `FromSelect` return `ErrValidation`, and so does a model without a table schema in its generated metadata (the array types come from it). Int, float, bool, string, `time.Time` and `[]byte` columns bind as typed slices (`[]*T` when a value is NULL); any other element type (uuid, json, decimal, named enums) falls back to `[]any`, which pgx may reject for an array type, so use plain `Models` for such a model. `OnConflict`, `Upsert` and `Returning` work as for `Models`; interceptors, `BeforeInsert`, field validators, automatic timestamps and id generators run as for `Models`. A `FlagSensitive` column's array shows as `RedactedArg` in `QueryEvent.Args`.
- `Merge` is PostgreSQL 15 or later; `.Returning` needs 17 or later. An older server or a driver without `ServerVersioner` returns `ErrUnsupported` before the statement runs. SQLite, MySQL and MariaDB have no MERGE: `Exec` runs the clauses as temporary-table copies of the source and of the matched pairs, an `UPDATE` and an `INSERT` in one transaction (a savepoint inside a `Tx`), which gives PostgreSQL's final table and affected-row count without concurrent writers (it takes no lock against a matching row committed between its steps); a target row that two source rows match is `ErrTooManyRows` (on PostgreSQL too), `Returning`, `SET col = DEFAULT` and a matched update on a model without a primary key are `ErrUnsupported`, and `MergeQuery.Statements` lists the statements because `SQL` has no single text there. It needs `On` and at least one WHEN clause (`ErrValidation`). An interceptor that adds predicates makes it fail with `ErrValidation`, because they cannot be applied to a MERGE; deny the kind instead. Field validators do not run on the values inserted from the source.
- `BulkUpdate` and `BulkUpdateKeys` (a composite key) update only the keys in their row list, bind one parameter per value, and keep the version and updated-at columns current. They run on PostgreSQL, SQLite, MySQL and MariaDB (`UPDATE ... FROM` on the first two, `UPDATE ... JOIN` on the MySQL family). `Exec` splits a list over the parameter limit into chunks that run atomically (a transaction on a `DB`, a savepoint on a `Tx`); `SQL` and `Rows` render one statement and return `ErrLimitExceeded` over the limit. `Returning` needs a dialect with `UPDATE ... RETURNING`, so MySQL and MariaDB return `ErrUnsupported`. `RowsAffected` counts the rows that match a listed key on every dialect, changed or not.
- `Truncate` is `TRUNCATE TABLE` (no `RESTART IDENTITY`, no `CASCADE`), and `DELETE FROM` plus a sequence reset on SQLite. It runs the interceptors with the kind `truncate`, which a tenant-scoped handle should deny, and MySQL refuses it inside a transaction.

Raw SQL (escape hatches; the SQL text must be a constant, pass user input only
as arguments):

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
// Predicate fragment:           ?  binds the next argument, ?? is a literal ?, @name binds momo.Named("name", v)
momo.Select[models.Task](q).Where(momo.SQL(`lower("tasks"."title") LIKE ?`, "%go%"))
// Typed expression for Set/Columns/OrderBy:
momo.TypedSQL[int64]("balance + ?", delta)
// Statements and scalar lists:
affected, err := momo.Exec(ctx, q, `UPDATE tasks SET done = ? WHERE id IN (?)`, true, momo.In(ids))
ids, err := momo.QueryScalars[int64](ctx, q, `SELECT id FROM tasks WHERE done = ?`, true)
// Several columns into Row1..Row10 (positional), a model or a projection (matched by column name):
rows, err := momo.Query[momo.Row2[int64, string]](ctx, q, `SELECT id, title FROM tasks WHERE done = ?`, true)
for row, err := range momo.QueryRows[momo.Row2[int64, string]](ctx, q, `SELECT id, title FROM tasks`) { _, _ = row, err }
// Helpers: momo.In(slice) (empty slice is a build error), momo.Ident("col"), momo.SubquerySQL(sql, args...)
```

- DON'T build SQL text with `fmt.Sprintf` from user input. Use `?`, `In`, `Ident`.
- QUALIFY column names in raw fragments inside joined or preloaded queries
  (`"tasks"."title"`): Momo qualifies its own columns, and an unqualified name
  becomes ambiguous with a joined table. A column qualified by a table that is not
  in the statement's FROM/JOIN is `ErrValidation` at build time.
- On PostgreSQL write `? |` with a space for a bind followed by OR; `?|` and `?&`
  are operators. On PostgreSQL a fragment may use native `$n` placeholders instead
  (see "Porting pgx and sqlc SQL" below); do not mix them with `?`/`@name`.
- Returned results of raw queries bypass soft-delete, hooks and timestamps.
- `Query[T]` (buffered, `[]T`) and `QueryRows[T]` (streaming `iter.Seq2[T, error]`)
  are the multi-column raw read, for a hand-written `SELECT` or `... RETURNING`.
  `T` is `Row1`..`Row10` (positional: the result must have exactly that many
  columns) or a model or projection (matched by column name in any order, exact
  then case-insensitive; an unmapped, missing or duplicated result column is
  `ErrValidation`). `T` may also be a plain struct with no generated metadata
  (no generator run, any number of columns): its exported fields are the
  columns, named by a `momo:"column:x"` tag or else the column name the DB's
  naming preset gives the field (`momo.New(drv, momo.WithNaming(naming.Prisma{}))`;
  snake_case without the option: `UserID` is `user_id`, `RoleIDs` is `role_ids`,
  `HTTPServer` is `http_server`), `momo:"-"` skips
  a field, the fields of an embedded struct count as the outer struct's own
  (unless it is a `time.Time`, a `sql.Scanner` or has a column tag; an outer
  field shadows an embedded one, two fields on one column and an embedding
  cycle are `ErrValidation`; an embedded pointer struct is allocated for every
  row and stays non-nil even when all of its columns are NULL),
  and a pointer field receives NULL as nil (NULL into a non-pointer field is
  the driver's scan error). Names compare exactly, then case-insensitively. The
  reflection plan is built once per type and cached
  (`BenchmarkQueryPlainStruct`). A type with generated metadata (a model, a
  projection, `Row1`..`Row10`) always uses it, and a type that is neither is
  `ErrValidation` before the statement runs. By-name matching needs every
  result column to map to a field and every field to be in the result (the
  error names the column or field), so `SELECT d.*, count(*)` needs a struct
  with a field for each result column.
  Placeholders, hooks (op `raw`), error classification and
  argument redaction are those of `Exec`; interceptors, soft-delete filters and
  `AfterLoad` do not apply to raw SQL. `QueryRows` closes the cursor on early
  break, on an error and on a canceled context (`ErrCanceled`).
- `QueryCursor(ctx, q, sql, args...)` returns the open cursor (`momo.ColumnRows`:
  `Next`, `Scan(dest...)`, `Columns`, `Err`, `Close`) for a result whose shape is
  only known at run time. It has the hooks (op `raw`), `WithTxSetup`,
  error classification and redaction of `Query`, on a `*DB`, `*Tx` or `AdoptTx`
  handle. Always close it: an unclosed cursor holds its connection (and, under
  `WithImplicitTx`, its transaction). A canceled context closes it and `Err` is
  `ErrCanceled` (also when the cancel came after the last row, as in
  `QueryRows`). Under `WithImplicitTx` raw SQL counts as a write: reading to the
  end commits, and a `Close` before the end (even with no `Next`), after a Scan
  or driver error, or after a cancel rolls back and returns `ErrValidation`;
  without it an early `Close` is plain. Scan errors are classified and recorded
  on the hook event. `Columns` is the driver's list: empty means no columns (an
  `UPDATE` without `RETURNING`) or an unnamed driver. Prefer `Query[T]` when the
  shape is known.

#### The raw SQL family

Nine functions of the root package take hand-written SQL. They share one
placeholder contract (`?` binds the next argument, `??` is a literal `?`, `$n`
on PostgreSQL, `momo.In`, `momo.Ident` and `momo.Named` as arguments) and one
safety rule: the SQL text is a trusted constant and user input is an argument.
They fall into two groups.

Functions that run a statement take a context, a querier, the SQL text and its
arguments, hit the database at once and have hooks with the op `raw`:

| Function            | Returns                           | Use it for                                                |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `momo.Exec`         | rows affected, error              | a statement that writes or changes the schema             |
| `momo.Query`        | `[]T`, buffered                   | a result whose row type is known                          |
| `momo.QueryRows`    | `iter.Seq2[T, error]`, streamed   | the same result without buffering it                      |
| `momo.QueryScalars` | `[]V`, one column                 | a single-column result such as ids                        |
| `momo.QueryCursor`  | `momo.ColumnRows`, an open cursor | a result whose shape is known only at run time (close it) |

Functions that wrap a fragment for a builder take no context, run nothing and
return a value that another builder renders:

| Function             | Returns              | Use it for                                                    |
| -------------------- | -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `momo.SQL`           | `momo.Predicate`     | a condition in `Where`, `Having` or `On`                      |
| `momo.TypedSQL`      | `momo.Expression[T]` | a value in a select list, an assignment or a typed comparison |
| `momo.SubquerySQL`   | `momo.Subquery`      | a SELECT used in `IN`, `EXISTS`, a CTE or a set operation     |
| `momo.CompilableSQL` | `momo.Compilable`    | a hand-written statement registered with `momo.RegisterQuery` |

The naming rule: a function that runs hand-written SQL is a verb (`Exec`,
`Query`, `QueryRows`, `QueryScalars`, `QueryCursor`); a function that wraps
hand-written SQL for a builder ends in `SQL` (`SQL`, `TypedSQL`, `SubquerySQL`,
`CompilableSQL`). No name carries the word Raw.

#### Porting pgx and sqlc SQL

On the PostgreSQL dialect, raw SQL (`Exec`, `QueryScalars`, `Query`, `QueryRows`, `SQL`, `TypedSQL`,
`SubquerySQL`) accepts PostgreSQL's native `$1, $2, ...` placeholders, so a
statement written for pgx or sqlc moves over unchanged:

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
// pgx / sqlc:   pool.Exec(ctx, "UPDATE tasks SET done = $1 WHERE owner = $2 OR creator = $2", true, uid)
affected, err := momo.Exec(ctx, q, "UPDATE tasks SET done = $1 WHERE owner = $2 OR creator = $2", true, uid)
```

Rules:

- `$n` binds positional argument n of that call. A reused `$n` (here `$2`) binds
  the argument once. An `In`, `Ident` or `Expr` argument is rendered again at each
  use. Momo renumbers: inside a larger statement (`TypedSQL` or `SubquerySQL`
  after earlier `Where` binds) `$1` still means the fragment's first argument.
- One style per fragment. Mixing `$n` with `?`, `@name` or `Named` is
  `ErrValidation`.
- Every `$n` needs an argument (`$3` with two arguments, or `$0`, is
  `ErrValidation`) and every argument must be used (a gap such as `$1, $3` is
  `ErrValidation`), so a typo fails at build time.
- A `$n` inside a string literal, quoted identifier, comment or dollar-quoted body
  is text, not a placeholder.
- Other dialects: `$n` is `ErrUnsupported` at build time on SQLite and MySQL,
  even when the fragment has no `?`. Port such statements to `?` (or `@name`)
  when the code must run on SQLite or MySQL.
- A literal `$n` that must reach the server as text, as in `PREPARE` or a
  `CREATE FUNCTION` body that refers to its parameters, is read as a placeholder
  and fails with `ErrValidation` for a missing argument. Put it where momo
  treats it as text: inside a string literal or a dollar-quoted body, for example
  `DO $$ BEGIN EXECUTE 'PREPARE p AS SELECT $1::int'; END $$`.
- Behaviour change: before native `$n` support a `$1` in raw PostgreSQL SQL went
  to the server untouched. It is now a momo placeholder, so a statement that used
  `$1` as text needs the treatment above.
- sqlc `sqlc.arg(name)` / `@name` styles: use `momo.Named("name", v)` with `@name`.
- Typed casts keep working: `$1::int` is fine.

`SelectQuery.SQL()` returns `Compiled{SQL, Args}` without running. `Explain(ctx)`
runs `EXPLAIN` (never `ANALYZE`) and returns plan text; it binds parameters and
does not execute the query. Inside a `Tx`, it sees that transaction's settings.
`momo.Explain(ctx, q, compiled)` plans any statement's `Compiled` (writes
included, PostgreSQL, SQLite, MySQL and MariaDB) and `momo.ExplainAnalyze(ctx, q,
compiled)` runs it under `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` (PostgreSQL only; always rolled
back, but a rollback cannot undo `nextval`, `NOTIFY` or `dblink` effects). Momo never calls either on its own; see [observability](observability.md).

Select-time guards: `Limit`/`Offset` negative is `ErrValidation`.

Details: README sections 5-7, [capabilities.md](capabilities.md).
Examples: [crud-zero-null](../examples/crud-zero-null/),
[projection-pagination](../examples/projection-pagination/).

### Writing your own expression

Code outside the root package builds typed expressions with a small frozen
extension API, listed with the reason for each name in the
[compatibility policy](compatibility.md#the-expression-extension-api). Writing
one correctly means identifiers go through `Builder.Ident` and values through
`Builder.Arg`, never concatenated into the SQL.

- `momo.Ops[T]`: embed it in your struct to make the struct an `Expression[T]`
  (a `Predicate` when `T` is `bool`) with `Eq`, `Ne`, `Lt`, `Le`, `Gt`, `Ge`,
  `IsNull`, `IsNotNull`, `Between`, `In`, `NotIn`, `Asc` and `Desc`.
- `momo.NewOps[T]`: binds the embedded `Ops` to the finished struct. Call it in
  the constructor, as the example below does. An unbound `Ops` fails the
  build with `ErrValidation`.
- `momo.Typed[T]`: wraps any `Expr` as an `Expression[T]` without comparison
  methods, which is how a predicate that has no methods of its own is built.
- `momo.Flagged`: the column flags of an expression. Give your expression a
  `Flags() momo.ColumnFlags` method that returns the flags of the wrapped
  column (assert `momo.Flagged` on it, or return 0) so a sensitive column stays
  masked in hook events when you compare through the `Ops` methods.
- `Builder.Ident`, `Builder.Arg`, `Builder.WriteString`, `Builder.Dialect` and
  `Builder.SetErr`: identifiers, values, the fixed SQL text, the dialect being
  rendered, and the build error. Call `SetErr` with a `*momo.Error` of kind
  `momo.ErrUnsupported` for a dialect that cannot express the feature.

A value you bind with `Builder.Arg` yourself is not masked beside a sensitive
column; compare through the `Ops` methods when an operand can be one. The
helpers the Momo subpackages (`agg`, `fts`, `jsonop`, `sqlfn` and the others)
use beyond this list are internal and not available to you.

```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"github.com/azrtydxb/momo"
)

type shout struct {
	momo.Ops[string]
	src momo.Expr
}

func newShout(src momo.Expr) shout {
	s := shout{src: src}
	s.Ops = momo.NewOps[string](s)
	return s
}

func (s shout) AppendSQL(b *momo.Builder) {
	b.WriteString("upper(")
	s.src.AppendSQL(b)
	b.WriteString(")")
}

func (s shout) Flags() momo.ColumnFlags {
	if f, ok := s.src.(momo.Flagged); ok {
		return f.Flags()
	}
	return 0
}

// newShout(col) works in Columns, Where (newShout(col).Eq("X")) and OrderBy.
func main() {
	title := momo.NewColumn[string]("documents", "title", 0)
	_ = newShout(title).Eq("X")
	fmt.Println("ok")
}
```

DON'T build the SQL text from caller input with `WriteString`; use `Ident` and
`Arg`. A tested version is the `NewOps` example in `expr_extension_example_test.go`.

## 7. Transactions

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
err := db.Tx(ctx, momo.TxOptions{}, func(tx *momo.Tx) error {
	// use tx (a momo.Querier), NOT db, for everything in here
	if _, err := momo.Update[models.Account](tx).
		Set(account.Balance.SetExpr(momo.TypedSQL[int64]("balance + ?", amt))).
		Where(account.Owner.Eq(to)).Exec(ctx); err != nil {
		return err // any error (or panic) rolls back
	}
	return nil // nil commits
})
```

- `db.Tx(ctx, opts, fn)` commits on nil, rolls back on error or panic. `fn` runs
  exactly once; Momo never retries it.
- DON'T use `db` inside the closure: it runs outside the transaction on another
  connection and can deadlock on a small pool.
- `TxOptions{ReadOnly: true}` makes the server refuse writes (SQLSTATE 25006;
  Momo has no sentinel for it: `errors.As(err, &pgErr)` with
  `*pgconn.PgError`). `TxOptions{Isolation: sql.LevelSerializable}` sets the level;
  supported: read uncommitted, read committed, repeatable read, serializable. Any
  other level is `ErrUnsupported`.
- Savepoints: `tx.Tx(ctx, func(sp *momo.Tx) error {...})` runs in a savepoint; if
  it fails only its work is undone and the outer transaction continues. Without a
  savepoint PostgreSQL aborts the whole transaction at the first error. Manual:
  `tx.Savepoint(ctx, name)`, `tx.RollbackTo(ctx, name)`, `tx.Release(ctx, name)`.
- Manual control: `tx, err := db.Begin(ctx, opts)`, `tx.Commit(ctx)`,
  `tx.Rollback(ctx)`; a finished `*Tx` returns `ErrTxDone`. Prefer `db.Tx`.
- Incremental adoption in a `database/sql` or pgx codebase, both directions:
  - Adopt a transaction the caller began: `mtx := db.AdoptTx(pgxdriver.SQLTx(sqlTx))`
    for a `*sql.Tx` (database must be pgx-stdlib backed, `pgxdriver.NewSQL`), or
    `db.AdoptTx(pgxdriver.PgxTx(pgxTx, opts...))` for a `pgx.Tx` (pgxpool driver; `opts` are the options of `New`, such as `WithExecMode`; an unsupported exec mode returns `ErrUnsupported` on use, as with `New`). An adopted `pgx.Tx` keeps Batch and `COPY`; an adopted `*sql.Tx` has neither. Statements,
    hooks, error classification and savepoints (`mtx.Tx`) work as usual. `Commit`
    and `Rollback` on `mtx` return `ErrAdoptedTx` and do nothing: the caller
    commits or rolls back its own transaction. After that, `mtx` statements
    return `ErrTxDone`. A nil argument panics.
  - Expose the handle behind a `*Tx` to legacy helpers:
    `pgxdriver.UnwrapSQLTx(tx)` returns `(*sql.Tx, bool)` and
    `pgxdriver.UnwrapPgxTx(tx)` returns `(pgx.Tx, bool)`; `false` when the `Tx`
    belongs to the other driver kind. Works for `db.Tx` callbacks, adopted
    transactions and savepoint scopes (the outer transaction). Finish a
    momo-begun transaction through momo, never through the unwrapped handle.
  - Mixing is safe: a legacy `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` helper and momo statements
    can alternate on the same transaction.
- Do not call blocking network I/O inside `fn`.
- Retry the WHOLE `db.Tx` on `ErrSerialization` (PostgreSQL 40001 serialization
  failure and 40P01 deadlock). Only when `fn` has no side effects outside the
  database. Copy of `examples/transactions`:

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
func retrySerializable(ctx context.Context, db *momo.DB, fn func(tx *momo.Tx) error) error {
	const (
		maxAttempts = 3
		backoff     = 20 * time.Millisecond // doubles in a real service
	)
	var err error
	for attempt := 1; attempt <= maxAttempts; attempt++ {
		err = db.Tx(ctx, momo.TxOptions{Isolation: sql.LevelSerializable}, fn)
		if !errors.Is(err, momo.ErrSerialization) {
			return err
		}
		if attempt == maxAttempts {
			break // out of attempts: return the error without sleeping
		}
		d := backoff/2 + rand.N(backoff) // math/rand/v2: jitter so competitors do not collide in lockstep
		select {
		case <-ctx.Done():
			return ctx.Err()
		case <-time.After(d):
		}
	}
	return err
}
```

- On a pinned connection (`db.OnConn(pc)`) transactions are not available:
  `Begin`, `Tx`, `Replace`, `CreateGraph` return `ErrUnsupported`.
- Several momo helpers open their own transaction on a `*DB` and a savepoint on a
  `*Tx`: `Replace`, `CreateGraph`, chunked `InsertQuery.Models`, `vecsearch.With`.

- Publish an event together with a data change through the transactional
  outbox (which databases it runs on, and how the relay wakes on each, is in
  [outbox](outbox.md) and the generated [capabilities](capabilities.md)):
  declare the outbox table as a model, call `outbox.Outbox.Add(ctx, tx, event)` with the
  `tx` that writes the data, and run `outbox.Relay.Run` with a `outbox.Publisher`
  you implement. Delivery is at least once, so consumers deduplicate on
  `outbox.Event.ID`; events with the same key keep their order. See
  [outbox](outbox.md).

Details: README section 8. Example: [transactions](../examples/transactions/).

## 8. Relations

Declare with tags (section 4). Relations never load by themselves: a plain
`Select` leaves relation fields empty. Relation descriptors (`document.Comments`)
are immutable and concurrency-safe.

Decision table:

| Need                                                        | API                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Children for rows you already fetched                       | `momo.Load(ctx, q, parents, rel, opts...)`: one statement per relation, not per parent                                                                                                                                 |
| Several relations for the same parents                      | `momo.LoadAll(ctx, q, parents, rel1, rel2.Scope(opts...), rel3.Then(nested...))`                                                                                                                                       |
| Filter, order and nest one relation                         | `rel.Scope(where, orderBy).Then(nested)` with `LoadWhere` and `LoadOrderBy` options                                                                                                                                    |
| Load as part of a query (`All`/`One`/`First`)               | a select query's `.Preload(rel, ...)`                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Belongs-to with no extra round trip                         | `Preload(rel.Joined())`: LEFT JOIN in the parent statement                                                                                                                                                             |
| Only some children, ordered, top-N per parent, soft-deleted | `rel.Scope(opts...)` with `LoadWhere`, `LoadOrderBy`, `LoadPerParentLimit`, `LoadWithDeleted`, `LoadOnlyDeleted` (each generic over the child type, as in the example below; `Load` accepts the same options directly) |
| Children of children                                        | `rel.Then(nested...)`                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Filter parents by children                                  | `Where(rel.Has(scope...))`, `rel.HasNo(...)`, `rel.HasFrom(parentAlias, ...)`                                                                                                                                          |
| Order parents by child count                                | `OrderBy(rel.CountOrder(momo.DirDesc))`                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Children matching a parent query, no parent fetched         | `rel.From(parentQuery)` returns `SelectQuery[C]` (not many-to-many)                                                                                                                                                    |
| Add or remove links to EXISTING rows                        | `rel.Link(ctx, q, &parent, &c1, &c2)`, `rel.Unlink(...)`, `rel.Count(ctx, q, &parent)`                                                                                                                                 |
| Make the linked set exactly this one                        | `rel.Replace(ctx, q, &parent, children...)`                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Insert a parent and NEW children together                   | `momo.CreateGraph(ctx, q, &parent, rel1.Include(), rel2.Include())`                                                                                                                                                    |
| Get-or-insert on a unique key                               | `momo.FindOrCreate(ctx, q, []momo.ColumnRef{author.Name}, &a)` returns `(created bool, err)`                                                                                                                           |
| Insert or update by primary key                             | `momo.UpsertByPK(ctx, q, &m)`                                                                                                                                                                                          |

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
docs, err := momo.Select[models.Document](db).
	Preload(
		document.Author.Joined(),
		document.Comments.Scope(
			momo.LoadWhere[models.Comment](comment.Approved.Eq(true)),
			momo.LoadOrderBy[models.Comment](comment.ID.Desc()),
			momo.LoadPerParentLimit[models.Comment](3)),
	).
	Limit(20).All(ctx)

withApproved := momo.Select[models.Document](db).
	Where(document.Comments.Has(comment.Approved.As("momo_r").Eq(true))) // child alias is momo_r

err = document.Tags.Link(ctx, db, &doc, &models.Tag{ID: 1}, &models.Tag{ID: 2})

doc := models.Document{Title: "Hello", Author: &models.Author{Name: "Ada"},
	Comments: []models.Comment{{Body: "first"}}}
err = momo.CreateGraph(ctx, db, &doc, document.Author.Include(), document.Comments.Include())
```

Rules and limits:

- `Load`/`LoadAll`/`Preload` clear the association first, so a parent with no
  children is empty (nil), never stale. NULL-key parents get an empty
  association. Parent order never changes.
- `Scope(...)` and `Then(...)` combine: both return a `RelationLoader` with
  `Scope` and `Then` methods, so
  `document.Comments.Scope(approvedOnly).Then(comment.Author)` (with
  `approvedOnly` a `momo.LoadWhere[models.Comment]` option) filters the comments
  and loads each one's author in one loader. The options
  apply to that relation's children only; nested loaders carry their own; the
  nested level runs over the surviving children only (one statement per level).
- `Joined()` is belongs-to only, and only when the child key is the child's
  primary key or a single unique column. Has-one, has-many, many-to-many give
  `ErrUnsupported`. `momo.Load(ctx, db, docs, X.Joined())` does not compile
  (`Joined()` returns a `Loader`, `Load` wants a `Relation`; cannot infer `C`),
  and `LoadAll` returns `ErrUnsupported`. Also `ErrUnsupported` with
  `Then`, `GroupBy`, `Having`, `ForUpdate`, `Each`, `Iter`. With `Columns` the
  select list must have one expression per mapped field (`ErrValidation`).
  Qualify raw column names in the parent's `Where` (ambiguity with the joined
  table).
- `LoadPerParentLimit(n)`: has-many and many-to-many only (belongs-to and has-one
  `ErrUnsupported`); `n < 0` is `ErrValidation`; 0 is unlimited. `LoadWhere`
  filters before the limit.
- `Has`/`HasNo` predicates must name the child column through the alias
  `momo_r`: `comment.Approved.As("momo_r").Eq(true)`; an unaliased column refers
  to the OUTER table. `Has`/`HasNo` nest: each level has its own child alias
  (`momo_r`, `momo_r2`, `momo_r3`; join table `momo_j`, `momo_j2`), the inner one
  correlates on the enclosing alias, and `As("momo_r")` in a scope always means
  that scope's own level. `As(momo.RelAlias(n))` names level n explicitly (1 is
  the outermost) and is never rewritten. A nested `Has` in a self-reference
  correlates on the enclosing child; `HasFrom(alias)` keeps the alias given. Do
  not name your own aliases `momo_r<N>` or `momo_j<N>`.
- Has-one that matches several children for a parent: `ErrTooManyRows`.
- `Link`, `Unlink`, `Replace`, `Count` write SQL directly: model hooks, field
  hooks and `UpdatedAt` are NOT run. Use the model's update path when those must
  run. They never modify the values you pass.
- Many-to-many `Link` relies on a primary or unique key over the join columns.
  Join tables generated from `many2many` tags have one. A hand-written join table
  needs a unique key, or `Link` inserts duplicates.
- Has-one/has-many `Unlink` and `Replace` clear the foreign key: it must be
  nullable, else `ErrNotNullViolation`. Delete the children instead if they cannot
  exist without a parent.
- Belongs-to is not linkable: all four helpers return `ErrUnsupported`. Set the
  foreign key field on the parent and `Update` it.
- NULL parent key (or NULL child key on many-to-many) is `ErrValidation` for
  `Link`/`Unlink`/`Replace`; `Count` returns 0. `Link`/`Unlink` with no children
  are no-ops.
- `Replace` is a transaction (`*DB`) or savepoint (`*Tx`) and locks the parent row
  (`FOR UPDATE`), so concurrent `Replace` on one parent serialize. `Link`/`Unlink`
  take no lock and may interleave. On a `*Tx` the lock lasts until your
  transaction ends. A non-existent parent locks nothing.
- `Link`/`Unlink` needing several chunks are atomic on a `*DB` (one
  transaction); on a `*Tx` a later chunk failing leaves earlier chunks applied
  until you roll back.
- `CreateGraph`: one level deep; always INSERTs (never matches existing rows);
  belongs-to children first, has-one/has-many after the parent, many-to-many
  children inserted then linked; hooks, timestamps and defaults run. On a `*Tx` it
  runs in a savepoint. Nil parent, a model as its own child, or a NULL key that
  must be copied: `ErrValidation`. Has-many and many-to-many children go in as
  chunked bulk inserts (1000 children = one statement). Keys are read back with
  `RETURNING` (MariaDB: `INSERT ... RETURNING`); MySQL has none and reads
  `LAST_INSERT_ID` after each statement, so its children go in one row per
  statement inside the graph's transaction (never guessed consecutive keys:
  `innodb_autoinc_lock_mode` 2, the MySQL 8 default, does not guarantee them);
  children that mix zero and explicit keys are `ErrValidation` there and a
  non-integer generated key is `ErrUnsupported`. A dialect with neither
  `RETURNING` nor `LAST_INSERT_ID` gives `ErrUnsupported` before a transaction
  opens. DON'T list a
  many-to-many relation whose children are already stored: they are inserted
  again and fail with `ErrUniqueViolation`; use `Link` for existing rows.
- `FindOrCreate` needs a UNIQUE constraint on exactly the key columns. It
  overwrites your struct with the stored row when it exists; a soft-deleted
  row is not found, it fails with `ErrUniqueViolation`. Under REPEATABLE READ/SERIALIZABLE the re-select can return
  `ErrNotFound`: retry the transaction. Empty key or unmapped column:
  `ErrValidation`. On MySQL and MariaDB it runs in a transaction as a plain
  insert and, when that hits a unique violation, a shared-lock select by key
  (a failed insert plus a select when the row exists; a no-op
  `ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE` cannot tell created from found under
  `clientFoundRows`).
- Tag-declared relations: `belongs_to` needs a single-column primary key on its target (the referencing model may have a composite key containing the fk column); `has_one`/`has_many` need one on the parent; `many2many` on both.
- A pipelined load buffers a whole level's child rows (about twice the memory of
  sequential). An unscoped load of a huge has-many is expensive: scope it.
- Many-to-many to self and join tables with extra columns are not supported by tag;
  use an explicit join model struct for extra columns.
- Parent keys are chunked under the bind limit automatically; `WithMaxParams(n)`
  lowers it for tests.

Details: [relations.md](relations.md). Example: [relations](../examples/relations/).

## 9. Vectors

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
type Item struct {
	momo.Model `momo:"table:items"`
	ID         int64         `momo:"pk,identity"`
	Title      string        `momo:"size:200"`
	Category   string        `momo:"size:50,index"`
	Embedding  vector.Vector `momo:"dim:1536"` // dim = your embedding model's output size
}

func (i *Item) MomoConfig(c *momo.Config) {
```
